## Session 21e: sideload, remove, compact and the upgrade

12 November 2026 · branch `claude/s21e-sideload-remove-compact-1c6511` · [#127](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/127) · upstream `4c252c33`, unchanged

Phase 3's round 5 on the server track, the S21 group's third row on the web, after S21d, beside S24b upstream, on PLAN's defaults, with S21d's follow-up folded in: a Standalone server's search answers while a job writes its index, the second half of the owner's choice B of 11 November, which closes the line S21d's done-when moved to that follow-up. A Standalone server serves its own index through the kit's live read-only opens; side-loads a volume's TEI file, listed by the catalogue overlay when the catalogue lacks it and cited with the app's sentence; removes an indexed volume through a job; compacts, checks and resets its index; and at a start re-indexes an index behind the kit's date-index version while search answers. SPEC's Operating modes ▸ Standalone mode's indexing (its served-index bullet) and the new Standalone mode's upkeep and side-load are the whole account; this entry says what was built where, the decisions, how the done-when is shown, what the reviews changed, and what S21f and S21g take from it. The branch was cut from `main` at `b7e1e27`, #125's merge, and the work was kept in local commits until the push; no file of the app changed and no migration was added.

**The live stack** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/ServedIndex.swift`, `IndexWriting.swift`, `Sources/FRUSLightCore/IndexImport.swift`, `ServerState.swift`), S21d's follow-up, through the opens FRUS-Explorer#1897 put in the pin:
- `CorpusIndex.open(_:live:)` opens a Standalone server's index through `FTS5Store.readOnlyURI(for:)`, `?mode=ro` without `immutable`, at the start, after an import that seeds it and after each job; it is marked `isLive`, and `ServedIndex` then opens `FTS5Store(readingLiveDatabaseAt:)`, `IndexingPipeline(readingLiveIndexAt:…)`, with the user store attached as before, and the page-range, person and cross-reference stores' `init(databaseURL:…)`. Import mode keeps every immutable open and its swap: `live` is false by default, the importer's `liveReads` and the start's open follow the mode, and the stack branches on `isLive`.
- A live open's version is its documents' own record, the lowest `document_revisions.index_version` of a document the index holds (`ExportChecks.checkLiveVersions`, the kit's own `EXISTS` in `document_cache`, so that the revisions it keeps of removed volumes count for nothing), refusing an index with a document of a later version; the export's stamp is no longer the version of an index the server has indexed into.
- `ServedIndexWriting` serves the index while the indexing job writes it: after each volume and at the job's end it opens `CorpusIndex` again and serves it, so that the counts, the volumes a working corpus resolves against and the stack's caches follow each volume. A job that holds the index to itself names why (`willWriteIndex(at:holding:)`, `ServerState.indexHold`): a compaction, and a reset while it empties the index; meanwhile search answers 503, `INDEX_BEING_WRITTEN`, in its sentence, and `/readyz` `indexing_library`, as S21d's indexing did. S21d's `indexWriteUnfinished` is gone: a log a reader keeps from folding at a job's end is read through, and folded by the next job or start. The provider lets go of released stacks as it opens new ones.

**The side-load** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/AdminLibrary.swift`, `Sources/FRUSLightCore/Library.swift`, `UserLibrary.swift`, `ServerResources.swift`): `POST /api/v1/admin/library/sideload?file=<name>` in a group of its own, whose guard takes XML (`UserDataGuard.mediaTypes`) of 64 MiB at most, the route refusing past the limit as it streams. The name gives the id by the app's rule, the name less `.xml`, and only a name of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, beginning with a letter or digit, of 128 characters at most and no other volume's figures folder or sidecar (`VolumeLibrary.sideloadedVolumeId(fromFileName:)`). The upload goes to a hidden staging folder, which a start removes; the kit's `SideloadValidator` reads it into a folder of the library's own, where it is flushed, and it takes its name by `link(2)`, which refuses a name taken meanwhile, so that the duplicate check and the placing are one step; the store keeps the row `sideloaded = 1`, with its hash, length and time and no figures (`recordLibrarySideload`, on both stores). A volume the catalogue lacks needs a header the kit's `LocalVolumeCatalog` reads. Its indexing is a job, `.asked`. FoundationXML on Linux resolves no external entity with the kit's parsers' defaults and libxml2 stops an entity that expands without end (error 89), measured in the build image before any code and held by a test and the smoke test, so no gate of the server's own was added before the kit's parsers.

**The catalogue overlay** (`ServerResources`): `LocalVolumeCatalog.reconcile(in:known:)` at each Standalone start and after each side-load and removal, the later of two refreshes kept; `volume(_:)` answers for a side-loaded volume as the app's `ManifestStore.entry(forVolumeId:)` does, so the reader, Browse (listed after the catalogue's, `sideloaded`), the Library (`catalogued`, false) and every route that names a volume take it, and Citation Lookup, Add Documents' citations and the cross-reference store read the published catalogue alone, as the app's `citableEntries` and `bundledEntries` do (#1523). A side-loaded volume's citation, its records and the reader's document carry no history.state.gov link, and the citation carries the app's sentence, the server's (`citation.sideloaded.note`, held to the app's).

**The index's upkeep** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/IndexUpkeep.swift`, new, `Sources/FRUSLightAPI/AdminIndex.swift`, new, `AdminStatus.swift`), each a job of the indexer's, the index's one writer:
- **Remove** of an indexed volume (`libraryRemove`): the kit's `removeVolume(_:)`, the server's record and the sentinel forgotten, the passes after indexing, the log folded, the index opened again, then `VolumeLibrary.remove(_:)`, which now takes a side-loaded id and its sidecar; the removal kept in the stamps from its first write until its files are gone, finished by the next start; a second removal of a volume refused; one that fails forgotten. The route's `VOLUME_INDEXED` refusal is lifted where an indexer is.
- **Compact** (`indexCompact`): `vacuumIndex()`, holding the index to itself, once the data volume has the room this server's copy needs, twice the live size and 64 MB, checked through a live read-only open before the hold; whether a compaction is worth offering is the app's `IndexCompaction`, mirrored as `IndexCompactionRule` (`IndexUpkeepParityTests`). **Check** (`indexCheck`): `checkIndexIntegrity()` while search answers. `GET /api/v1/admin/index` gives the room.
- **The pass over every volume:** an upgrade and a reset re-index with the kit's `indexAllVolumes()`, as the app's launch and its Rebuild From Scratch do, which rebaselines revisions rather than stamping them, the index served and opened again after each volume as the kit's progress stream says it stored it, a volume that fails kept failed with the stage its pass reached; it runs to its end once begun, as the app's does.
- **Reset, Standalone's** (`indexReset`, `POST /api/v1/admin/index/reset`): `removeAllVolumesFromIndex()` under the hold, the stamps forgotten (`indexWasReplaced(sameFile:)`, the side files kept), then the pass; kept in the stamps until the pass ends, so that a stop's cut is finished at the next start.
- **At a start** (`prepareAtStart`, before the index is opened): the writer's open migrates the schema; full-text tables of an earlier generation are rebuilt from the cache before the index is served (`rebuildSearchIndexFromCache()`); a cut-short reset is emptied again; a cut-short removal's index part is finished, then its files; and when the stamps' date-index version is behind the kit's (`installedDateIndexVersion`, a stamp of 0 reading as the documents' lowest), an upgrade begins, which the start's job, the pass, does while search answers and `/readyz` names the volumes still to go; the stamps are the kit's once the pass has run, whatever failed, as the app marks them. Before an import replaces a Standalone index, its log is folded (`indexWillBeReplaced`).

**The decisions:**
- **The upgrade and the reset run the kit's pass over every volume,** not the indexing job's `indexVolume` a volume at a time, which the first draft used: `indexVolume` stamps a document's change, and a document an earlier parse left out that a later parse emits again would read as changed by an update; `indexAllVolumes()` is how the app re-indexes after a version bump and after its wipe, rebaselining, and the kit has no public single-volume rebaseline. So an upgrade a stop cuts short is begun again by the next start, whose pass takes every volume again, as the app's launch runs its pass again, and the pass takes no cancel once begun, as the app's takes none. A volume the index holds with no file in the library, as a seeding export's can be, is outside the pass and keeps its version until it is downloaded and S21f's Update indexes it.
- **Compaction's room is the server's own,** twice the live size and 64 MB: SQLite's temporary copy is on the data volume (`SQLITE_TMPDIR`), and the copied pages go to the log as well, where the app's 1.15 times the live size, which the pane's words keep, is the margin for its own temporary folder.
- **No gate of the server's own before the kit's parsers:** the kit's parsers' defaults on Linux already resolve no external entity, and libxml2 stops an expansion that runs away, both shown in the image; a gate would refuse files the app takes.

**How the done-when is shown:**
- A side-loaded fixture volume is read and cited with the sentence: `LibraryUpkeepRouteTests.aSideloadedVolumeIsReadAndCitedWithTheAppsSentence` (a copy of frus1894Nicaragua under an id the catalogue lacks: its row, the Library, Browse, the reader, search and its citation with the app's sentence and no link); and the smoke test's library step, in the image.
- A volume removed is gone from search, Browse and the reader: `aRemovedVolumeIsGoneFromSearchBrowseAndTheReader`; the smoke step removes the two it side-loaded.
- The smoke test compacts and checks: its library step, after the removals, the index's file smaller and its check passing; `theIndexIsCompactedAndChecked` in Swift.
- A run killed between volumes is finished at the next start, in a test: `IndexUpgradeTests.anUpgradeAStopCutShortIsFinishedAtTheNextStart`, the first server stopped inside its pass and the next start's pass finishing every volume; `aResetAStopCutShortIsFinishedAtTheNextStart` and `aRemovalAStopCutShortIsFinishedAtTheNextStart` for the other two.
- A volume indexed under a lowered stamp is re-indexed at start: `aVolumeIndexedUnderALoweredStampIsReindexedAtTheStart`, `/readyz` naming the volume still to go while the index is served.
- S21d's moved line, a search during indexing answers: `LibraryIndexingRouteTests.searchAnswersWhileAJobWritesTheIndex`, S21d's test turned around, a search held inside a volume's pass finding its documents while the kit names it unfinished; and the smoke step, whose search answers 200 between two readings of Status naming the indexing job running.

**Also shown:** the side-load's refusals, a name for each rule, the media type, the length and the stream (`theSideloadRefusesWhatIsNoVolume`); its external entity and entity bomb (`aSideloadedFilesExternalEntitiesAreNeverRead`); the library's side-load whole or not at all and the store's row on both stores (`SideloadTests`); full-text tables of an earlier generation rebuilt at the start; Standalone's reset (`aStandaloneResetEmptiesTheIndexAndIndexesTheLibraryAgain`); a second removal refused; the compaction's rule and the citation's sentence held to the app's source (`IndexUpkeepParityTests`); and the new routes refused to a reader (`AdminRouteTests`). In the browser app, `web/src/admin/Upkeep.test.tsx`.

**Two cold reviews,** subagents given the diff and the points the row asks a review to weigh, and none of this session's reasoning: one of the server and its tests, one of the browser app, the smoke test and the records. What held up was fixed before the push:
- **The upgrade could never finish, and stamped changes no file made** (server): the first draft re-indexed with `indexVolume`, kept a failed volume pending for good, and stamped a returning document as changed; the upgrade and the reset now run the kit's pass, above.
- **Removed volumes' revisions held the live version down** (server): the version now counts documents the index holds.
- **Two removals of one volume could be queued,** the second wedging it (server): the indexer refuses the second in the step that takes the first, and a failed removal is forgotten.
- **A reset a stop cut short left the full-text tables empty** (server): the reset is kept in the stamps and finished at the next start.
- **Compaction's room was the app's margin** (server): the server's own, and checked before the hold.
- **An import replacing a Standalone index could leave the old log beside the new file's name,** which a live open would read (server): the log is folded before the install.
- **Two overlay refreshes at once could keep the older listing** (server): the later is kept.
- **The browser's caches never followed the index** (browser): the shell reads again what it reads of the index when `/readyz`'s sentence changes, and a side-load and a removal ask again what Browse and search read.
- **Download Again for a volume the catalogue lacks; Index All Waiting counting what the server will not take; buttons marked unavailable that acted; a removal under way not shown** (browser, server): the Library gives `catalogued` and `removing`, the route counts the overlay's volumes, and the pane guards what it marks.
- **The smoke's poller could die at one missed reading, and the compaction's check showed nothing** (smoke): the poller survives, and the compaction must shrink the file.
- **The records** said more than the code: Browse's mark, the compaction's time, the reset's search, the error codes, which the docs now say as the code does.
- Left as they are, each said where it matters: Citation Lookup and the cross-reference store read the published catalogue alone, as the app's do (#1523); and a volume a seeding export holds with no file keeps its version through an upgrade, for S21f.

**The runs before the push,** at `5e73f1b`, each in one hold of `heavy.sh`; after them only the records changed, and the words of one line the smoke test prints:
- CI's swift job, `scripts/swift --postgres test`, this package's own targets built clean: the build in 86 s with no warning; 3,756 tests, CrossRefKitTests 10, FRUSCoreKitTests 2,159, FRUSLightCoreTests 271, FRUSLightServerTests 345, FRUSParityTests 251, FRUSRichTextTests 42, FTS5CheckTests 3, FTS5StoreTests 219, GeneratorKitTests 7, ManifestGeneratorTests 60, SemanticVectorsKitTests 40, SourceExplorerExportGeneratorTests 22 and SourceNoteKitTests 327, this row's 16 among them (`IndexUpgradeTests` 5, `SideloadTests` 3, `LibraryUpkeepRouteTests` 6, `IndexUpkeepParityTests` 2) with S21d's test it turned around, and the one skip the job allows, `backupExclusion()`. Three issues, none this row's: two tests of the user store on PostgreSQL, `UserLeadsTests.leadsAreKeptAsTheAppKeepsThem` and `UserSummaryTests.aSummaryFromAResearchDatabaseMayBeDeletedButNotChanged`, were refused a connection, "sorry, too many clients already", the limit of 100 clients Session 21d's entry describes, and `FRUSLightCoreTests` with PostgreSQL then passed twice running, 271 tests each; and `RelatedDocumentsParityTests.aSeededProjectsLeadsAreTheAggregators` read a Project Home holding the leads of the computation before the one it waited for, 23 where the kit gives 24, the suite then passing twice running alone (Found in passing, below).
- CI's web job, through `scripts/npm`: `ci`, typecheck, lint, test (564 tests in 61 files) and build.
- `FRUS_IMAGE=frus-light:s21e FRUS_PARITY_IMAGE=frus-light:s21e-parity FRUS_HOST_PORT=18260 scripts/compose-smoke --e2e`: PASS. The library step's search answered 200 six times while the indexing job wrote the index, each between two readings of Status naming the job running; a volume was side-loaded under an id the catalogue lacks, listed from its header, indexed and cited with the app's sentence and no link, and a file's external entity read nothing of the image's; the two side-loaded volumes were removed, the index compacted from 6 MB to 5 MB and checked; check 2 passed over the Standalone index; and the browser suite passed, 82 tests at the root and 82 under the path, with the library spec's Standalone test on the Standalone server.
- **CI's compose job on the first push** failed at the side-load's first check, which looked for the answer's `volumeId` before its `catalogued`: the server's JSON keeps its keys in no set order, each process drawing its own, and the Mac's run had drawn that one. Each key is now looked for alone, and the Library's listing, read once the side-load's job has ended, also says the volume is not catalogued; the smoke test passed again over `frus-light:s21e`.

**Found in passing, not this row's:** Project Home (`ProjectHome.swift`'s `GET …/home`, S23d's) reads its rows, the leads among them, then awaits the leads' snippets through the served index, and only then the computation's state, so that a Refresh ending in that window answers `succeeded` beside the earlier computation's leads, and a browser that stops polling on `succeeded` shows them: the parity test's 23 are the first computation's 24 with the dismissed lead hidden. Reading the state before the rows closes it; it is a follow-up's, since the file is not this row's.

## Session 24b: the person maths, Chronology and About the Series, upstream

12 November 2026 · branch `claude/s24b-person-chronology-records-52f4cf` · [#126](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/126) · upstream `4c252c33`, unchanged; [FRUS-Explorer#1899](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1899), open

Phase 3's row S24b, the second pull request of the third upstream batch: the person maths, the co-mention network's choice of nodes and edges, Chronology's rules and About the Series' data into FRUSCoreKit, for S24f to S24h. The pull request is `claude/person-chronology-series-into-kit`, cut from `v2` at `b0ab1027`, #1898's merge, which `v2` still is. It is labelled `Mac`, its body asks for Mac verification and lists Mac check 22, and it is not merged. Under rule 4 it changes shared files, and this repository changes only its records.

**What moved,** by `git mv`, at 100% in the first commit: `SeriesProductionData.swift`, `PublicationLagTarget.swift`, `SeriesGeographyData.swift`, `SourceProvenanceData.swift`, `AdministrationProfilesData.swift` and `SeriesAxisRange.swift` (the series charts' year range) from `FRUSExplorer/SeriesAnalytics/` to `FRUSCoreKit/Analytics/Series/`; `ChartInspectorAdapters.swift`, About the Series' tables, to `FRUSCoreKit/Analytics/Export/` (Foundation-only, reading only the kit's types once the data types are the kit's, so the row's "take it if small" held); `TaxonomyModels.swift` (`TagTaxonomyEntry`, with `VolumeLevelTag` and `TagCategory`) to `FRUSCoreKit/Models/`; and nine suites (below). `AdministrationProfilesData.swift` lost SwiftUI: `PoliticalParty.color` stays the app's, unchanged, in `SeriesAnalytics/PoliticalParty+Color.swift`.

**Out of files that stay:** `PersonTrajectoryNormalization`, `PersonTrajectoryPoint`, `PersonAnalyticsMath`, `PersonRelationshipPoint` and `PersonRelationshipMath` out of `PersonAnalyticsView.swift` into `FRUSCoreKit/Analytics/PersonAnalyticsMath.swift`, unchanged but for access and `Sendable`; `PersonCoMentionNode`, `PersonCoMentionEdge` and the view model's choice of nodes and edges out of `PersonCoMentionGraphView.swift` into `PersonCoMentionNetwork.swift` (`partnerLimit`, the two halves of `load(from:volumeIds:)`'s reading of the store, `partners(of:focusRollupId:)`, `capApplied`, `capDisclosure`), the view model's names forwarding and its `load` calling the two halves in turn, so a failed edge query leaves the nodes in place as before; `ChronologyDateGroup` (its memberwise initialiser spelt out and public), `ChronologyOverflowCounts`, the four constants and every static rule of `ChronologyViewModel` into `FRUSCoreKit/Chronology/ChronologyGrouping.swift` as `enum ChronologyGrouping`, line for line, the view model keeping its state and `reload()`, its names forwarding. `IndexingPipeline.documentsInDateRange` and `dateBucketVolumeCounts` are public, unchanged.

**Loading by URL:** `SourceProvenanceIndex(contentsOf:)` and `AdministrationProfilesIndex(contentsOf:)` decode the two aggregates at a URL as the app's `SourceProvenanceStore` and `AdministrationProfilesStore` decode the bundled copies, as the kit's other bundled indexes have done since S22a. The two stores are `@Observable @MainActor` classes over `Bundle.main`, which the kit's boundary rules keep out (no bundle, no Observation), so they stay the app's, unchanged; a host loads the indexes by URL.

**#1896 and the administration presets:** S24a's #1896 did not move `AdministrationProfilesIndex`, since `CorpusAnalyticsService` does not read it: Corpus Analytics' presets are `AdministrationPresetMenu.presets(from:corpusMaxYear:currentYear:)`, a SwiftUI file's static. This pull request makes the index and `AdministrationProfile` the kit's, which that rule reads, so S24f decodes the bundled index with the kit and mirrors the presets' rule (or asks for it upstream).

**The suites,** by `git mv` into `FRUSExplorerTests/FRUSCoreKit/`, every suite whose subject moved, what needs the app inside `#if !SWIFT_PACKAGE` (tests in Xcode; in the package): `PersonAnalyticsTests` (60; 18, the co-mention graph's view model, layout, labels and the host's focus Xcode's), `ChronologyQueryTests` (42; 39), `SeriesProductionDataTests` (9; 9), `SeriesGeographyDataTests` (13; 13), `SourceProvenanceDataTests` (29; 21), `AdministrationProfilesDataTests` (29; 24), `PublicationLagTargetTests` (7; 7), `SourceProvenanceScopeTests` (11; 10) and `SeriesAxisRangeTests` (9; 9): 150 of their 209 tests in the package. `ChartDataInspectorTests`' adapter tests and `AnalyticsExportTests`' trajectory periods join them there. `SeriesTestSupport.swift` gives the package the two series stores over the repository's copies and `ChronologyViewModel`'s statics over the kit's rules. New: `PersonCoMentionNetworkTests` (5) and `SeriesIndexLoadingTests` (4). No moved suite sets the process's time zone. The app's scans follow the moved copy (five CountCopy baseline entries, the archival copy guard, `AppSourceTree`'s key), and 25 EditableContent blocks are re-pointed with the amendment log's entry.

**Two cold reviews,** given the diff and none of this session's conclusions, one on Apple behaviour and one on the kit, Linux and the suites, during the branch's first run. Neither found a behavioural change in the app. The fixes: a moved suite's `#filePath` root one folder short (the first iOS run's one extra failure); a kit-only suite swallowed by a guard, and `AnalyticsExportTests`' trajectory periods still Xcode's alone; the co-mention cap's EditableContent block interpolating `\(partners.count)`, which a write-back would put out of scope in the kit's function; a stale note and three `ships at` lists there; and `ChronologyDateGroup`'s initialiser, which a host needs to narrow a section as the app's legend filter does. Kept, and said in the pull request: `load` now reads the focus once, when it starts, where it read it again after each `await`; that differs only if the focus changes mid-load, which the hidden controls prevent.

**How it was checked,** each heavy job under the app's lock, from the clone at a real path, Xcode 27.2, clean and unsigned, on the iPhone 17e simulator (iOS 27.2), beside `v2` at `b0ab1027` built and run the same way:
- **Mac:** both build with `v2`'s 2 and 3 warning lines, line for line. The symbol diff: 257,142 normalized names on `v2` and 257,217 here, 87 removed and 162 added, every one in a group the pull request names (the moved bodies under `ChronologyGrouping` and `PersonCoMentionNetwork`, the two enums, the two loaders, two await points of `load`, renumbered thunks).

## Session 21d: indexing on the server

11 November 2026 · branch `claude/sad-greider-f4235c` · [#121](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/121) · upstream `68bffcf6`, unchanged; [FRUS-Explorer#1897](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1897), open, awaiting Mac check 25 · records [#122](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/122)

**Since merged** (S23c's pin move records it): the upstream pull request, [FRUS-Explorer#1897](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1897), merged on 11 November (22:24 UTC) as `4c252c33`, whose tree is its head's, `b36e1db0`, onto `v2` at `782127ff`, so Mac check 25 is done. S23c's pin move took it, so the follow-up that serves the index while a job writes it starts at the pin.

Phase 3's round 4 on the server track, the S21 group's second row on the web, after S21c, beside S23d and, upstream, S24a. A Standalone server indexes the volumes its library downloads into its own index, with FRUSCoreKit's read-write pipeline, in jobs of the server's queue, keeps the kit's stamps in a file beside the index, keeps each volume a pass did not index with the stage the kit's stream gave, and stops between volumes when cancelled. SPEC's new section, Operating modes ▸ Standalone mode's indexing, is the whole account; this entry says what was built where, the two decisions, how the done-when is shown, what the reviews changed, and what S21e to S21g take from it. The branch was cut from `main` at `2a0f10a`, #115's merge, after #117, and the work was kept in local commits until the push.

**The kit had no read-only open without `immutable`.** PLAN's row serves a Standalone index "read-only without `immutable`", so that search reads each volume as its store commits. At the pin and at `v2`'s head `9e6cc2af`, `FTS5Store(readingDatabaseAt:)` and `IndexingPipeline(readingIndexAt:…userStore:)` open `?mode=ro&immutable=1` alone; their other opens are read-write, and the user store's attach, which every signed-in search reads (S17d), is the immutable open's alone. `PageRangeStore(databaseURL:)` and `PersonMentionStore(databaseURL:)` already read without it. An immutable reader of a file in write-ahead-log mode reads the main file with no lock and never the log, so it sees a stale index, and torn pages once a checkpoint runs: no web-side way round it is correct. The orchestrator put two orders to the owner, who chose B on 11 November: this row merges with a Standalone server's search refused while a job writes, and a follow-up serves the index while it is written, once a pin move carries the kit's new opens. So **the done-when's "a search during indexing answers" moves to that follow-up, by the owner's choice of 11 November.** The upstream pull request is part of B, and is Mac check 25: FRUS-Explorer's branch `claude/live-read-only-index-opens`, cut from `v2` at `9e6cc2af`, adds `FTS5Store(readingLiveDatabaseAt:schema:)`, with `FTS5Store.readOnlyURI(for:)`, and `IndexingPipeline(readingLiveIndexAt:fts5Store:resources:volumesDirectory:userStore:)`: `?mode=ro` without `immutable`, the user store attached as on the immutable open, the immutable and read-write opens as they were, and nothing the app calls. `IndexReadOnlyOpenTests` shows the live open, beside a writer that keeps the file open, answering as the writer does, seeing a volume indexed after it opened, its documents before its pass finishes, refusing every write and refusing what the immutable open refuses; `SearchUserSourceTests` shows its attach. The kit's suites pass on the Mac over it, `FRUSCoreKitTests` 2,049 tests in 261 suites and `FTS5StoreTests` 219. Its pull request, [FRUS-Explorer#1897](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1897), opened after this one, rebased onto `v2`'s `782127ff` (#1896) before it opened, with the whole check at its head `b36e1db0` beside `v2` there, in one hold: both app builds with `v2`'s warning lines; the iOS unit run on the iPhone 17e, 7,970 tests in 958 suites against 7,966, failing only where `v2` fails, the same 17 tests and 2 suites skipped; `swift test`, 4,118 tests in 492 suites against 4,114, `FRUSCoreKitTests` 2,159 in 276 against 2,155; the Mac symbol diff, 16 names removed and 25 added, all in the initialisers it changes; and Linux over `main` `c227009`, 3,690 tests against `v2` alone's 3,686, with the same 24 issues in the parity suite, line for line, and the access proof compiled. The live test, run with the immutable opens in its place, fails at the open, "schema generation 0": the writer's schema is still in the log. With `v2` alone over the same copy of `main`, `RelatedDocumentsParityTests.aSeededProjectsLeadsAreTheAggregators` fails, value for value as with the branch, beside the 23 issues the pin move settles (21 golden files made from the pin's sources, and 2 reads of the file #1891 moved); S24a saw it pass with `9e6cc2af` over `2a0f10a`, so the next pin move meets it. A records-only pull request, #122, named it here.

**The decision: what queues the indexing.** S21c's hand-over weighed two hooks: an indexing job queued when a download job ends with volumes downloaded, or a job reading `library_volumes` for files whose blob SHA differs from what the index last took. The first is taken: a download job that fetched volumes, however it ends (succeeded, failed in part, cancelled or stopped by a host), queues a job for every volume that waits, by the kit's own list (`volumesAwaitingIndex(excluding:)`), those whose last pass failed left out unless the download fetched them again. The queue runs one job at a time, so the indexing runs once the download has ended, and a job asked for while another waits joins it. The second hook needs what the index last took of a file, which nothing records yet: the corrections check (S21f) compares blob SHAs with the listing's, and its Update downloads and then indexes through this job. Two more queue a job: a start, once the index found there is open, for what waits, less a volume whose pass a stop of the server cut short, which the kit's sentinel names, as the app's launch leaves such a volume to its reader; and an admin's Index.

**The stamps** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/IndexStamps.swift`), `IndexStampFile`, the kit's `IndexingStampStore` over `/data/index/index-stamps.json`: what the app keeps in `UserDefaults` (the date-index and FTS-schema versions, the rollup's version, fingerprint and date-index version, the broken-references index applied, and `IndexingStateTracker`'s sentinel), read back as the kit's `InMemoryIndexingStampStore` reads them, with the server's record of each volume a pass did not index (`IndexingFailureRecord`: failed or stopped, the stage, the sentence, when). Each change writes the file whole under a hidden name, `fsync`s it, renames it over the old and `fsync`s the folder, under one lock, so a restart reads it as it was before a change or after it; a failed write keeps the change in memory and is made again with the next. A file that cannot be read is set aside, and the stamps begin again, which makes the kit's gated passes run again. An import that installs an export in the index's place clears them (`IndexerAfterIndexImport`).

**The job** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/LibraryIndexing.swift`), `LibraryIndexer`, built at every start and wired in `ServerComponents.make`, `libraryIndex` beside the queue's other kinds:
- It waits for the index a start found to be opened, refuses to write an index the server does not serve (one the start refused), opens the kit's read-write `IndexingPipeline` with the stamps and the tracker, turns on `setStopsBetweenBatchesWhenCancelled(true)`, and takes the kit's list of what waits.
- Each volume is a step: a cancel between volumes stops it there. The pass runs in a task group beside a watcher of the job's cancel, which cancels the pass so that S21a's stop ends it once its documents are stored; the volume is then kept as stopped, `storingTables`, and the next indexing finishes it. A volume is not begun when the data volume would keep less than 64 MB free beyond twice its file.
- The kit's `progressStream` is read as it comes (`IndexingProgressRelay`): its updates say the job's line, reading the XML, then storing the documents and the other tables, and its last stage before `.failed` is kept with a volume that fails, the sentence the server's: the parser's error and where, never a path. A SQLite failure that means the index cannot be written stops the job, the rest not tried.
- Then the passes after indexing, `runPostIndexPasses`, over what was indexed, a cancel's job included, and the date-index and FTS stamps set to this build's after a first pass, as the app sets them, since every index this server serves is at the kit's version.
- The writer is let go at the end, its connections closing, and the job folds the write-ahead log into the file with `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` through a connection of its own, before the served index is told.
- `Library.swift` (S21c's) tells it the volumes each download job fetched (`whenDownloadsEnd`), on every way the job ends.

**The served index while a job writes, B** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/IndexWriting.swift`, `ServedIndex.swift`, `ServerState.swift`): before the job's first write, `ServerState.indexBeingWritten` is set, and the provider lets go of its stack and waits, five minutes at most, until no request holds one, by weak references to the stacks it opened. Meanwhile every route that reads the index answers 503, `INDEX_BEING_WRITTEN`, a plain refusal naming the indexing, `/readyz` answers a new step, `indexing_library`, which the browser app's banner shows, and the reader renders from the volumes' files, as it does with no index (`servedIfReady()` gives none). Once the job has closed the index, it is opened again (`CorpusIndex.open`) and served, `ServerState.indexWritten(_:)`, with the counts it holds now. Import mode is unchanged: the indexer refuses it, and the immutable open and the import's swap are as they were.

**The routes** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/AdminLibrary.swift`, S21c's): `GET /api/v1/admin/library` adds `indexing` (`active`, `volume`), a status `indexing`, and for a volume whose file is in place and whose last pass did not index it, `failed`, with `index` (`state`, `stage`, `at`) and `error` the server's sentence; `POST …/library/index`, `{"volumeIds": [...]}` or `{"all": true}`, 202 with the job, refusing a volume not in the library, one indexed whole (`VOLUME_INDEXED`), nothing waiting (`NOTHING_TO_INDEX`) and Import mode; and Remove refused while a job may index the volume (`INDEXING_IN_PROGRESS`). Status gives the job's line through S20d's `jobs.running`, unchanged.

**The browser app** (`web/src/admin/LibraryPane.tsx`, `web/src/api/library.ts`, `copy.ts`'s admin block): the Indexing state, **Index** on each volume that waits, **Index All Waiting**, a line naming the volume a job indexes, Download Again hidden while a pass reads a volume's file, and the Library read again every two seconds while an indexing job waits or runs; the job's kind, Library indexing; `indexing_library` among `api/types.ts`'s readiness steps.

**Compose, the image and the smoke test:** `docker/Dockerfile` gains a `parity` stage, built only when asked for, which builds `frus-parity` in the build stage's cache mount, so that once the server is built only the parity harness compiles, and which no release image holds. The smoke test's library step now waits for the downloads and the indexing after them, reads Status every twentieth of a second meanwhile, holds the one indexing job to "Indexed 3 volumes.", copies the Standalone index out, runs `frus-parity summarize` and `compare-summary` against `fixtures/golden/index-summary.json` in the parity image, then downloads a catalogue volume the mirror serves broken, `frus1964-68v01`, finds it listed failed while its XML was read, its job failed and the three still indexed, and removes it; the seed now waits for its import's job, since a Standalone server serving its own index answers `/readyz` throughout, and finds the export's volume indexed and one it lacks downloaded alone. `web/e2e/library.spec.ts` follows the re-downloaded volume to Indexed.

**How the done-when is shown:**
- Check 2's summary over the smoke test's Standalone index equals `fixtures/golden`'s: the smoke step, "check 2 passes: 36 digests and 7 checks are identical"; and `StandaloneIndexParityTests`, the job's index of the fixtures, "36 digests and 7 checks are the Mac's".
- A search during indexing answers: moved to the follow-up, by the owner's choice of 11 November. What this row shows instead: search answers 503, naming the indexing, while a job writes, `/readyz` says so, the reader renders, and search answers over what the job wrote once it ends (`searchWaitsWhileAJobWritesTheIndexAndTheReaderWorks`); the provider waits until no request holds a stack (`theProviderWaitsUntilNoRequestHoldsAStack`); and upstream, the live open sees a volume indexed after it opened, its documents before its pass finishes (`IndexReadOnlyOpenTests.aLiveOpenSeesWhatItsWriterCommits`).
- A volume that fails to parse is reported failed and the others indexed: the smoke step's broken volume; `aVolumeThatFailsToParseIsKeptFailedAndTheOthersAreIndexed`; `anAdminIndexesTheLibraryAndTheLibrarySaysHowEachVolumeWent`.
- The job's progress shows in Status: the smoke step's readings, "Status gave the indexing job's progress N times"; `statusShowsTheJobsProgressAndRemoveWaits`.

**Also shown:** the stamps read back through a restart, in their format, written whole while four tasks change them at once, a file that is not stamps set aside, a failed write made again (`LibraryIndexingTests`); a cancel between volumes (`aCancelStopsTheJobBetweenVolumes`) and within one, through the job's cancel, the volume left with its documents and no structure row and finished by the next indexing (`aCancelWithinAVolumeStopsItOnceItsDocumentsAreStored`); a start indexing what waits but the volume the sentinel names, which an admin's Index finishes (`aStartIndexesWhatWaitsButAPassAStopCutShort`); a download queuing its volumes' indexing (`aDownloadThatFetchedVolumesQueuesTheirIndexing`); requests joining the job that waits; a data volume short of room; Import mode and an unserved index left alone; an index replaced leaving no stamps; and the new route refused to a reader (`AdminRouteTests`).

**Two cold reviews,** each a subagent given the diff and the row's points to weigh, and none of this session's reasoning: one of the server, its tests and the upstream opens; one of the browser app, the smoke test and the Dockerfile. What held up was fixed before the push:
- **A log a stop left beside the index** (server): a stop mid-job leaves the write-ahead log, which the start's immutable open never reads, so the file would be served without its last commits, or with a page a checkpoint left half written; and an import renaming over the file left the old file's log beside it, which SQLite would read into the new file at its next read-write open. A Standalone start now folds such a log into the file before the open (`foldLogAtStart`); an import's install removes the old file's log and shared memory; and a job whose log cannot be folded keeps search refused, saying why, until a start folds it.
- **Remove could delete a volume the running job had indexed** (server): `holds` covered the volumes left to do alone, and under B the served index holds a volume only once the job ends. The job now holds its whole list until it ends, and every volume while it has not read its list, and the Library lists the volumes it has indexed as indexed.
- **A volume stored whole could stay failed for good** (server): a pass that threw after its store finished, as in the kit's FTS merge after it, or a stop between its last write and the sentinel's, left a record the kit's list never takes again. Such a pass now counts as indexing the volume, and an admin's Index settles a volume the index holds whole.
- **A volume that brought the server down would do so again after each download** (server): a download's job took the sentinel's volumes. It now leaves out a volume the sentinel names with no record of the server's own stop, unless the download fetched it again; an admin's Index takes it.
- **A request could be lost** (server): one slot for the job that waits let a second request overwrite the first's, whose job then fell back to every volume. Requests are kept by job, and a job whose request is lost takes a start's, the most careful.
- **The wait for readers could end while a computation still read the index** (server): a computation kept beside a search holds the stack's pipeline past the stack's last request. The provider now waits for each stack's pipeline too.
- **`image.yml`'s verify job would have failed on `main`** (smoke): the smoke test built frus-parity's image itself, where the verify job has no submodule and twenty minutes; and in CI's compose job a plain `docker build` would have used the engine's own builder, compiling the server again from nothing. Check 2's image is now `FRUS_PARITY_IMAGE`, which CI's compose job builds with `build-push-action` in the builder that built the image, whose cache mount then holds the server's objects; the script builds one beside an image it builds itself, and without either says that check 2 is skipped.
- **Focus** (browser): Index All Waiting, gone once nothing waited, took focus with it; and a reading of the Library that took a row's button away, as when the job takes the volume, dropped focus to the page, which the unit test missed, its stub changing the row inside the request, as the server never does. Index All Waiting now stays, unavailable when nothing waits; focus goes to the row when a reading takes away the button it was on; and the stub answers as the server does, the test following the job's poll.
- **Remove… was offered where the server refuses it** (browser): it is held while an indexing job waits or runs.
- **The library spec would meet `/readyz`'s 503** (browser): the shell reads `/readyz` while the job writes; the spec allows that reading's console error, the one it expects.
- Left as they are, each said where it matters: the person corrections, which the job's rollup leaves out (S21g's, below); the cooperative pool, on which the kit's pass and the rollup run, a thread each, so that on a one-CPU host requests wait while a volume is stored, where SPEC's hosts have two to four; a stop of the server mid-job, which the queue does not turn into a stop at a volume's end, leaving what the start folds and the sentinel names; and the parity image, which the smoke test leaves in place.

And the server's and the browser app's mirrors and the words held to the app's source.
- **The web unit suite,** from 536 tests in 56 files to 551 in 59: `relatedRules.test.ts`, `RelatedScreen.test.tsx` and `LeadsRefresh.test.tsx`.
- **The browser suite:** `related.spec.ts`, by keyboard alone: Related from the reader's toolbar, the heading focused; the scope by the arrow keys; a weight by the arrow keys, ranked again and kept in the browser, the slider keeping the focus; Reset, the focus back on Adjust weights; a row, and Back to the list as it was, where the index gives one; then a project with a note, whose Refresh finds its leads, Refresh keeping the focus; axe at each step. ## Session 21c: the library's downloads

11 November 2026 · branch `claude/xenodochial-zhukovsky-2e400a` · [#117](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/117) · upstream `68bffcf6`, unchanged

Phase 3's round 3 on the server track, the S21 group's first row on the web, beside S23d and, upstream, S22c, on PLAN's defaults. A Standalone server keeps its own library of volumes, downloads them, with their figure images, as jobs of S20d's queue, checks each file against GitHub's listing before it takes its place, resumes a download a restart stopped, and refuses all of it under `FRUS_OFFLINE`; an admin follows it in Administration ▸ Library. SPEC's new section, Operating modes ▸ Standalone mode's library, is the whole account of what it does; this entry says what was built where, the row's one decision, how the done-when is shown, what the reviews changed, and what S21d to S21g take from it. The branch was cut from `main` at `698b9db`, after #114, and the work was kept in local commits until the push.

**The decision: FoundationNetworking's `URLSession`, with libcurl added to the image.** PLAN wrote the downloads over FoundationNetworking before S25a found that the runtime image carries no libcurl, which FoundationNetworking's C half calls; S25a's note offered libcurl in the image or NIO, as `PDFService.swift` speaks HTTP. This row adds `libcurl4t64`, the OpenSSL flavour the build image links against, to the runtime stage, the one change to the Dockerfile's packages that rule 4 reserves to S20a and S20b, and says so here:
- PLAN's decision of 29 October is one HTTP client, FoundationNetworking's, for the downloads, NARA and Zotero, and S22c is moving the NARA and Zotero clients into FRUSCoreKit over it: from S23c's pin move the server links FoundationNetworking whatever this row chose, and a binary that links it does not start where libcurl is missing. The image needs the package by then either way.
- libcurl brings what a client written over NIO would have to: redirects (followed here within the host asked alone), chunked answers, HTTP/2, TLS with the image's CA certificates, and an outbound proxy, which a server behind one reaches through `https_proxy`: a probe in `swift:6.4-noble` with `https_proxy` naming a closed port failed on the proxy's port, so libcurl reads it. `PDFService`'s client suits one service on the Compose network; the library asks three public hosts.
- A probe in the build image before any code: `download(for:)` and `data(for:)` against GitHub's raw host and history.state.gov, a figure served as a PNG and a missing one answered 403, as the app's figure library says.

**Migration 7,** in both dialects: `library_volumes`, one row a catalogue volume the library has been asked for, with its download's `state` (`queued`, `downloading`, `downloaded` or `failed`), the file's `blob_sha` and `size_bytes`, `downloaded_at`, `sideloaded` for S21e, the figure images stored and refused, `error`, who asked and when, and when it changed. The store's methods are written once on `RelationalUserStore` (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/UserLibrary.swift`), `LibraryStore`: a queue that takes a volume once however often it is asked for while it waits, in one transaction; a download recorded, which keeps `downloaded_at` while the file is the one it named; a failure that keeps what the row says of a file in place; a withdrawal that puts a volume back as it was, `downloaded` when a file had taken its place, else no row; and the start's requeue of what a stopped server left. Every write is outside the search mark. No row is research: the export's list of tables that are no one's research and the daily backup's rule for a store that holds none leave the table out.

**The library** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/Library.swift`), `VolumeLibrary`, built at every start (`ServerComponents.make`), its folder made and checked in Standalone mode before the server listens:
- **Where it asks:** `LibrarySources`, GitHub's API for the listing, the kit's `downloadUrl` for a volume's file and history.state.gov's `frus/<volumeId>/<name>.png` for a figure, as the app's figure library names it; or, from `FRUS_LIBRARY_MIRROR`, the operator's alone, one folder served as the three hosts serve their files, each host's under its name. Nothing a request or a listing names becomes an address or a path.
- **How it asks:** `URLSessionLibraryTransport`, an ephemeral session whose delegate writes a 2xx body to its file as it comes, refused past the listing's length, flushed before the file is checked; keeps an error's first 64 KiB; follows a redirect within the host asked alone; and keeps nothing else. Under `FRUS_OFFLINE` the library holds no transport at all.
- **The job:** `libraryDownload`, registered beside the queue's other kinds. It reads GitHub's listing once, with the kit's `GitHubLiveEntry.volumes(inListing:)` and `ManifestDiffResult.diff(bundled:live:)`, a reading of the last five minutes used as it is and a later one asked with its ETag, and with `FRUS_GITHUB_TOKEN` to GitHub's own API alone; then each volume, a step each: its file written under a hidden name beside its place, kept only once its length and its git blob SHA-1, the kit's `VolumeUpdateChecker.gitBlobSHA1(for:)`, are the listing's, and renamed over the copy in place; a file in place that is the listing's is not asked for again. Then its figure images, by the app's scan, mirrored (`LibraryFigureNames`), each name a file name by the kit's rule, the image host asked nothing more in the job after three images in a row with no answer. A cancel stops the job between two volumes, putting back those it had not begun; a failed volume is said in its row and the job goes on, and three in a row whose host gave no answer stop it, as do a host's rate limit, a folder that cannot be written and a data volume that would keep less than 64 MB free. A start requeues what a stopped server left and downloads it in a job of the server's own, the volumes it had finished kept, after removing the hidden files a stopped download left.
- **The kit's corrections check reads it:** `VolumeLibrary` conforms to `DownloadedVolumeFiles`, its blob SHA-1 the one its download was checked by while the file keeps that length and modification time, taken again otherwise.

**The routes** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/AdminLibrary.swift`), registered in `AdminRoutes` beside the jobs', behind `/api/v1/me`'s guard and the admin role's: `GET /api/v1/admin/library`, every catalogue volume with its status, a download waiting or under way first, then a failure, then the index, then the file; `POST …/library/downloads`, some volumes or all, 202 with the job; and `DELETE …/library/volumes/{volumeId}`, refused for a volume the served index holds, whose leaving the index is S21e's. An Import server's Library lists its TEI folder and the index, and downloads and removes nothing (`LIBRARY_NOT_AVAILABLE`); a server under `FRUS_OFFLINE` answers `OFFLINE`. `FRUS_MODE=standalone` is accepted, with `FRUS_LIBRARY_MIRROR`, which only a Standalone server reads, and `FRUS_GITHUB_TOKEN`; `/readyz` of a Standalone server with no index says that an export seeds it.

**The browser app:** Administration ▸ Library (`web/src/admin/LibraryPane.tsx`, `web/src/api/library.ts`), between Jobs and Users, under the panes' library line: the catalogue's volumes found by id or title and shown by state, each with its state's words and why it failed, its file's size, when it was downloaded and its figure images; Download, Download Again, Download All and Remove…, which asks first, on a Standalone server; and the sentence that says why an Import or offline server downloads nothing. It reads again every two seconds while a download waits or runs. The words are in `copy.ts`'s admin block, beside the jobs', with the job's kind.

**Compose and the smoke test:** `compose.standalone.yaml`, used with `compose.yaml`, sets `FRUS_MODE=standalone` and replaces the services' volumes with Compose's `!override`, leaving out the read-only TEI mount, so that the server writes `/data/volumes` in its own volume; it passes `FRUS_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `FRUS_LIBRARY_MIRROR` and `FRUS_OFFLINE`. The image makes `/data/volumes` the server's user's, so that a volume an Import server used, whose TEI folder is mounted there, has a folder a Standalone server can write. The smoke test's new step, `== admin: the library, a Standalone project downloading from a folder served as GitHub serves it`, runs a Compose project of its own beside the main one, first in Import mode, then as a volume an older image left, whose folder is root's, refused and remedied as the install guide says, then in Standalone mode against an nginx serving a mirror of the three fixture volumes, GitHub's listing with their blob SHA-1s from `git hash-object`, and seven of frus1969-76ve09p1's eight figure images, the volumes served at 300 KB/s so that a restart lands mid-download; with `--e2e`, `web/e2e/library.spec.ts` runs alone there (`FRUS_E2E_LIBRARY`), and its Import server's test runs in the main suite.

**How the done-when is shown:**
- The smoke test runs a Standalone project that downloads the three fixture volumes, with their figures, from a folder served as GitHub serves them, and lists them: the smoke step, whose Library lists the three downloaded, frus1969-76ve09p1 with seven figure images and one refused, the reader rendering a downloaded document and serving a downloaded figure; and `theFixtureVolumesAreDownloadedWithTheirFigures` and `anAdminDownloadsListsAndRemovesVolumes` in Swift.
- A download interrupted resumes: the smoke step restarts the server once a volume is downloaded and the next is downloading, and finds the three downloaded after the start, the first job failed by the restart and a second, the server's, resumed, and the volume it had finished asked for once; `aDownloadAStopLeftIsResumedAtTheNextStart` in Swift, the hidden file a stop left removed.
- `FRUS_OFFLINE` refuses: the smoke step's offline start, whose download is `OFFLINE` and whose mirror is asked nothing; `offlineAndImportModeDownloadNothing` and `importModeOfflineAndAnIndexedVolumeAreRefused`.
- No byte of a volume differs from the fixture: the smoke step's SHA-256 of each downloaded file against the fixture's, and of each figure against the mirror's; `theFixtureVolumesAreDownloadedWithTheirFigures`, byte for byte.

**Also shown:** a file is kept only once its length and hash are the listing's, and a copy in place stays when its replacement fails (`aFileIsCheckedBeforeItTakesItsPlace`); a figure's name never reaches outside its folder, nor a link in its place (`noFigureNameReachesOutsideItsFolder`); a cancel stops between volumes (`aCancelStopsADownloadBetweenVolumes`); the listing's ETag, the token to GitHub's API alone and GitHub's limit (`theListingItsETagItsTokenAndGitHubsLimit`); Download All leaving out what the listing does not name; three unanswered volumes stopping a job; a host's rate limit stopping it, and an image host with no answer left (`aHostsLimitStopsTheDownloadAndAnImageHostThatDoesNotAnswerIsLeft`); an indexed volume's file downloaded once and not replaced (`anIndexedVolumesFileIsDownloadedOnceAndNotReplaced`); Remove; a folder the server cannot write keeping it from starting; the addresses the kit's and the app's; the store on both dialects (`theLibrarysVolumesAsTheStoreKeepsThem`); URLSession through libcurl against a live server, bounding, keeping an error's status and refusing a redirect to another host (`theTransportWritesBoundsAndFollowsWithinItsHostAlone`); a reader refused the three routes (`AdminRouteTests`); and the figure scan held to the app's source (`LibraryParityTests`).

**Two cold reviews,** each a subagent given the diff and the points the row asks a review to weigh, and none of this session's reasoning: one of the server and its tests, one of the browser app, the smoke test and the records. What held up was fixed before the push:
- **An Import install switched to Standalone did not start** (both reviews). Docker had made `/data/volumes` in the volume for Import mode's TEI mount, root's, which the server's user cannot write. The image now makes the folder the server's user's, so a new volume's is the server's under the mount; a volume an older image left is refused at the start with a sentence that gives the remedy, a one-off `chown` through `docker compose run` with `CHOWN` added, which the install guide gives too. The smoke test now starts its Standalone project on a volume an Import server used first, gives the folder to root as an older image's volume has it, finds the start refused with the sentence, runs the remedy and starts.
- **Download All's count** (browser) counted the volumes never asked for alone, so a failed one and an indexed one with no file were left out, and after a Download All, or a listing GitHub's limit refused, the pane said every volume was downloaded and offered nothing. It counts every volume whose file is missing and that no download holds, as the server takes them, and says when they all wait.
- **The image host** (server): a figure image with no answer took the request's minute, and never stopped the job, so a host that dropped every packet would hold the queue for hours. The job stops asking it after three images in a row with no answer, or one answer that it limits the server, as the app's pass stops after three volumes, and says so in each volume's row.
- **A file's hash** (server) was trusted while the file kept its length alone, the app's #1660 again: the row keeps the file's modification time too, and the hash is taken again when either differs, as the app keeps a hash with its file's stamp. An Import server leaves aside the rows a Standalone run kept.
- **GitHub's limit** (both): a 304 is free only with a token, as GitHub's guide says, and the records had said otherwise. A job within five minutes of the last reading uses it and asks nothing, and a host that says it limits the server, a 429 or a 403 with GitHub's rate-limit headers, stops the job rather than failing every volume after it.
- **A full disk** read as a host that gave no answer: a file that cannot be written stops the job, its sentence naming the folder, and a volume is not begun when the data volume would keep less than 64 MB free beyond it, room the user store and its backups share.
- **An indexed volume's file** could be replaced by Download Again under the index made from it: the route refuses it (`VOLUME_INDEXED`) until the corrections check, and the pane offers none.
- Smaller, all fixed: the transport's waiter could miss an outcome that came before it, as a task cancelled before it began has; a `.cancel` disposition, which FoundationNetworking on Linux may ignore, cancels its task too; a figure image is flushed before its rename, and one on disk is kept only when it opens as a PNG; Remove's check and its forgetting are one transaction; a resumed download leaves out what the listing no longer names, as Download All does; a mirror URL with a user or a password is refused and never echoed; a Standalone server with user data off says at its start that it downloads nothing; Remove says `LIBRARY_NOT_AVAILABLE` on an Import server before it looks at the index; the browser spec chose volumes the export indexes, and filtered by a prefix four volumes share; focus fell to the page when a download took its button; the status line was not cleared before a request; words offered Download where there is none; the Standalone spec's timeout; the install guide's `COMPOSE_FILE`, which hides `compose.override.yaml`, and the Compose release `!override` needs; and the smoke test's checksums, now sorted, and its mirror, now removed before its project. The first runs had found three of this session's own before the reviews: the kit's listing keeps files of 20,000 bytes or more, which the tests' small files fell under; four tests pinned the migrations at 6; and the smoke test read JSON by its keys' order.
- Left as they are, each said where it matters: HTTPS through the runtime image's libcurl and CA certificates is not tested, since the smoke test's mirror is http, though the build image's probe reached GitHub over https; a resource timeout, which FoundationNetworking may not enforce, is claimed nowhere; downloads run one at a time, as the job's steps need, so `FRUS_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY` is read by nothing (for S21g); and the listing's ETag is kept in memory, so a start's first reading asks afresh.

**Results**
- **Linux, `swift:6.4-noble`, arm64,** CI's swift job replayed with its PostgreSQL (`scripts/swift --postgres test`), under the heavy lock, this package's own targets rebuilt clean at `736a9d1`: 3,296 tests, every target passing but FRUSLightCoreTests, whose three issues the run found, all this row's tests: a restore test that pinned a newer store at migration 7, now 8, and a test that needed its clock moved past the listing's five-minute reuse (a third, which waited at a gate on a listing the reuse no longer asks for, had hung an earlier run). FRUSLightCoreTests then ran again whole with PostgreSQL at the fixes: 247 tests in 35 suites, all passing. Swift Testing's results hold one skip, check 1's Linux skip. FRUSLightCoreTests runs 247, FRUSLightServerTests 323, FRUSParityTests 235 and FRUSCoreKitTests 1,783; the row's suites are `LibraryTests` (16, the store's on both dialects among them) and `ConfigurationTests`' Standalone test in the first, `LibraryRouteTests` (5, URLSession against a live server among them) and `AdminRouteTests`' three new routes in the second, and `LibraryParityTests` (2) in the third. The tests that pinned migration 6 (now 7), the store's tables (`library_volumes` beside `jobs`), the export's tables that are no one's research and the backup's rule for a store that holds none follow this row.
- **The browser app:** typecheck, lint and build pass, and its unit tests, 540 in 57 files, 4 of them this row's (`web/src/admin/Library.test.tsx`).
- **The image and the smoke test:** `scripts/compose-smoke --e2e` with `frus-light:s21c`, this branch's image at `81193af`, on port 18200, passed every step: the library's, its volume an Import server's first, refused with the guide's sentence while its folder was root's and started after the guide's remedy, offline and refused with the mirror asked nothing, then downloading the three fixture volumes and seven figure images with a restart mid-download, every byte the fixture's and the mirror's, the reader rendering them and serving their figures, and an export seeding its index; the library spec on that Standalone server; 78 browser tests at the root and 78 under the path, the library spec's Import server's test among them; and the accounts and sign-in specs after them. The image's server links `libcurl.so.4`.
- **CI's compose job** then failed at the library's step on Linux, where the run on the Mac had passed: the step gave python3 the Library's answer, about 160 KB for the catalogue's volumes, as one argument, and Linux takes none longer than 128 KiB (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`), where macOS sets no such cap. The step's four reads of the Library now hand python3 a file. Checked on Linux, in the Playwright image's Ubuntu: an answer of 158,587 bytes as one argument fails as CI's did, and the script's own code, taken from `compose-smoke`, reads it from the file and passes.

**For S21g, the group's shared records** (PLAN's rule 5), from this entry:
- SPEC's configuration table: `FRUS_MODE`'s `standalone`, accepted; `FRUS_LIBRARY_MIRROR`, new, Standalone's alone; `FRUS_GITHUB_TOKEN`, read now, sent to GitHub's own API alone; `FRUS_OFFLINE` for a Standalone server, which serves what it keeps and downloads nothing; `FRUS_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY`, still read by nothing, since the job downloads one volume at a time so that a cancel stops it between two, to be dropped from the table or given a meaning. ## Session 21b, second follow-up: the reader opens every section the app's reader opens by its id

11 November 2026 · branch `claude/dazzling-faraday-5f5232` · [#125](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/125) · upstream `4c252c33`, #123's pin, unchanged here

The follow-up S21b's follow-up named ([#118](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/118), the entry below): its reader parsed alone only the sections Browse's Read opens, a back-of-volume index and a table of contents, so Previous and Next stopped at the lists the app's reader turns to as printed pages, and a table of contents' links to those lists and to its chapters found no page. Now the reader opens every section with an id of its own that the app's reader opens by that id, and Browse still links to the reader only what Read opens. Outside the plan's table, a pull request of its own, as #118's entry said; branched from `main` at `ff1b8c3`, #121's merge, with #118 and #120 in it, and merged with `main` before it was pushed, past S23c's pin move to `4c252c33` (#123) and again past #124, whose entry took this one's place in the log (Notes).

**The app's doors, at the pin.** Read before anything was designed. The app's reader opens any division by its id (`DocumentViewModel.load`, by `parseDocumentWindow` or `parseDocument(documentId:volumeURL:)`, which share the kit's `parseTarget`), from three places:
- **Browse's Read** opens a section the kit's `VolumeSection.canReadDirectly` passes; the persons and sources lists open views of their own (`FrontMatterPersonsView`, `VolumeSourcesView`). As #118 found it.
- **Previous and Next** turn through the kit's reading order (`DocumentViewModel.loadAdjacentEntries`, `IndexingPipeline.readingSequence`), and `mergeReadingSequence` puts in it every leaf of the outline with an id of its own (`hasExplicitSectionId`), from the index's row or, where it holds none, as an entry made from the section's title, and of a section that holds others only the row of its own text, where the index holds one. So a table of contents' Next is its volume's list of sources, whose Next is the list of abbreviations, then the list of names, then the first document.
- **A link** opens the reader on the id it names (`DocumentView`'s and `MacDocumentView`'s cross-reference taps, each a new entry with the id): a table of contents' entries name lists, compilations and chapters. A section the index leaves out for printing nothing of its own but its heading, the kit reads a second time, deciding nothing inside it, and gives whole but for its documents (`targetIsLeftOut`): a chapter's page is its heading, with the page breaks between its documents, and a compilation's is its heading and its chapters'. The reading order holds no such section, so its page has no Previous or Next.

**What the corpus holds,** measured for this entry over the owner's index of the 553 catalogue volumes from build 1812 (`frus-index-build1812-2026-11-10-all-vols.sqlite`, its outlines and rows) and, for the tables of contents' links, over the corpus's clone at `6170e4b32`; the scripts are not committed:

## Session 21b, follow-up: the reader opens a volume's index, and titles a document by its parsed head

11 November 2026 · branch `claude/pensive-chatterjee-427ea0` · [#118](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/118) · upstream `68bffcf6`, unchanged

Two follow-ups, outside the plan's table, in one pull request, each bringing the web's reader to the app's at the pin. S21b's pin move ([#107](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/107)) followed FRUS-Explorer#1875, whose back-of-volume index's "See" links scroll to their entry: the link route answers them (`indexEntry`) and the host script lands on them with the kit's `IndexEntryLanding`. Branched from `main` at `4580832`, #117's merge, with #107 and #108 in it.

**The app's door, at the pin.** Read before anything was designed:
- **Browse.** A section's row opens its page (`CompilationView`; on the Mac `CorpusSectionDocumentView`), whose Read button, "Read %@" with the section's title, opens the reader on the section's own id when the kit's `VolumeSection.canReadDirectly` passes: `CompilationDocumentsPresentation.resolve` routes it before anything else. The kit's parser captures a list the index leaves out whole, "so the reader can open it by id": a table of contents, an index, the persons and the sources.
- **What the same door opens.** Of the kinds Read opens (`proseReadableKinds`), the index promotes all but three (`promotableQuasiDocumentKinds`), and a full parse gives no document for those: `index`, `table-of-contents`, and `section`, which a division takes from its subtype, as frus1958-60v05mSupp's seventeen numbered sections do. So the door that opens the index opens a table of contents too, and those sections, by the same call, at no cost beyond the index's: done. The persons and sources lists it does not open, nor a list of another name, such as a subseries' list of volumes: left, as below.
- **The "See" references.** Over the corpus's clone at `6170e4b32`, the commit the app's own count is measured at (#1875: 49,799 in 397 volumes), a script of this session's (not committed) finds every one in a leaf section with an id of its own: 49,796 in a section of kind `index`, which Read opens, and three in frus1902app2's Table of Citations, a list of kind `citations`, which it does not.
- **The title.** The reader titles a document it parsed by the kit's `DocumentDisplayTitle` of `IndexingPipeline.extractHeader(from:)` over the parse, with its number, and one with no head and no note's shape by the title it was opened with: Browse's Read gives a section's title, so a section keeps it where its parse has no head. S25c's server already says this in `parsedTitle(of:)`.

**The server** (`Reader.swift`, `Catalog.swift`, `History.swift`, and `ReaderLinks.swift`'s comments):
- **Sections read alone.** `ReaderService.sectionsReadAlone(in:documents:)` is the sections of the TEI's structure that `canReadDirectly` passes and the full parse gives no document, in the structure's order, and each parse of a volume holds them. `document(volume:document:)` answers one with the kit's `parseDocument(documentId:volumeURL:)`, run the first time the section is asked for and kept beside the volume's parse while that is kept, with the volume's persons and terms, as the app's reader takes them from the TEI. A request that comes while it parses waits for that parse, a section read from an earlier file is never served beside a later parse, and an id that is neither a document nor such a section is `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`, as before. The page, its body, its rendering version, a highlight's version and Cite all reach the index and the table of contents through it.
- **Browse.** A section's `readable` on `/volumes/{v}` counts them, so the volume's contents link the index and the table of contents to the reader, as they link a preface.
- **The parsed head.** `DocumentDetail(teiOnly:)` heads a document the index does not hold by `parsedTitle(of:)`, S25c's `HistoryRoutes.parsedTitle`, moved beside the other naming rules in `Catalog.swift`, and keeps its label from the TEI, "Document 3" or a section's title, as its header and as its title where the parse gives none. History's visit title takes the same function and the same parse of a section alone, so the two agree: "3. Message From Chairmen Khrushchev and Brezhnev to President Kennedy" where the reader said "Document 3", and "Index" for the index. A section's list names such a document by the same head, so its row still reads as the heading it opens, as SPEC's Browse has it; its header stays "Document 3". The number is `ast.printedNumber` alone, as S25c's note says: the app's fallback, `extractDocumentNumber(from:)`, the first head that begins with a number, is still internal to the kit at the pin, and a title shows the difference only for a note with no `@n` whose first head names nothing, which no shipped document is.
