Phase 3's features-track row of wave 2, phase 2's follow-up to S18d, beside S20d, S22b and S23b, with no upstream pull request, no pin move and no migration: Add Documents' Citations and Tags tabs, over the kit code FRUS-Explorer#1814 made public at `fb542514`. None of the files the row reads changed between `fe9325b2` and the pin, `68bffcf6`: `CollectionAddDocumentsSheet.swift`, which holds `CollectionDocumentDiscovery`, and the kit's `CollectionCitationLineResolver.swift`, `CollectionGeneratedBlocks.swift` and `FRUSCoreKit/Citation/`.

**The kit's calls,** compiled from the submodule, none copied:
- `CollectionCitationLineResolver(parse:match:)` over the kit's `CitationParser` and the matcher Citation Lookup's routes ask, with `lines(from:)` and `resolve(line:)`.
- `CollectionGeneratedBlocks.tagDocumentRefs(tagId:noteTags:assignments:)`, the union of a tag's documents the Thematic Index reads too, over the user's notes and tag assignments.

**The store** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/UserTags.swift`): `TagStore.tagAssignments(of:)`, beside `tags(of:for:)`, written once on `RelationalUserStore` in SQL both stores read: every assignment of the user's as it was written, a `TagAssignmentRecord`, `ORDER BY rowid`. That is the order an export reads them in (`researchRows`), which the Thematic Index's assembly already hands the same union, and it stands for the app's fetch with no sort (`@Query`): an import writes a Mac's assignments in the order the Mac fetched them, and each made here after them. `created_at`, which the store's other reads of a document's assignments sort by, would put an assignment synced from another device where its time says, not where the Mac's sheet lists it.

**The server** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/AddDocuments.swift`, new; `CitationLookup.swift`; one line in `UserData.swift`, beside the collections' routes):
- **`POST /api/v1/me/add-documents/citations`** with `{"text"}` resolves each line the kit splits from the paste with the kit's resolver, one after another, and answers every line: its `outcome`, `resolved`, `ambiguous` or `unresolved`, and for the first two the document, the served index's head and the catalogue's volume title, with the resolver's note; for the last its reason, in the kit's words.
  - **The matcher is Citation Lookup's:** `CitationLookupRoutes.matcher(provider:resources:)`, drawn out of `add` so that both routes ask the same, the served index's or, with none served, the catalogue's alone.
  - **Bounded as Batch is:** 500 lines (`TOO_MANY_CITATIONS`) and a body of 256 KiB (`CONTENT_TOO_LARGE`), Batch's own constants. The resolver turns a lookup its task stopped into an unresolved line and goes on, so the route asks between lines, and reads the heads inside the same watched work: a paste whose client has gone stops at its next line.
  - **The heads** are the Research page's read of a document's title facts (`ResearchRoutes.titleFacts`, the app's `documentTitleFacts(for:)`), the documents' own rows a volume at a time, where the app's sheet reads `documentHeaders(for:)`, the same column.
- **`GET /api/v1/me/add-documents/tags`** lists the user's tags in `GET /me/tags`' order, each with the union's count over all their notes and assignments, whatever project they are filed under, as the app's sheet counts its rows. **`GET …/tags/{id}`** gives a tag's documents, the union's in its order, with heads and titles, and whether the catalogue lists each volume (`catalogued`); `TAG_NOT_FOUND` for a tag the user has none of.
  - **The union is the kit's,** over the store's notes (`notes(for:)`, newest first, as the app's editor queries them) and the new read of the assignments. For the list's counts each tag is handed its own notes and assignments, gathered in one pass: the kit passes over an entry that does not carry the tag it is asked for, so the answer is the one the whole lists give, which a test holds, and the counts cost one pass rather than one a tag. The work runs off the cooperative pool (`Blocking.run`).

**The browser app** (`web/src/collections/AddDocuments.tsx`; `addDocumentsRules.ts` and `api/addDocuments.ts`, new; `copy.ts`'s `addDocuments` block and the editor's footer; `styles/app.css`):
- **The tabs,** Search, Browse, Citations and Tags, in the app's order, one selection across them.
- **Citations:** the paste, in the app's monospaced field, with Resolve, which waits for text and for the last Resolve's answer. A status line says the app's count, "2 of 4 resolved · 1 to review", or "Nothing to resolve — paste at least one line.", or Resolving… while the server works. Every line has a row: one naming a document has its box, the app's words for the document, the line pasted, and the resolver's note, a warning on a line to review, which describe its box; one naming none says "No match — …" and has no box.
- **Tags:** the tags, each with its count, then a tag's documents, the focus handed to Tags and back to the tag, as Browse hands it.
- **Chosen at once:** what resolved, in line order, and a tag's documents as it opens, each pass passing over a document the reader unchose in the sheet, as the app's `preselect(_:)` does. A line to review waits for the reader.
- **The editor's footer** under Add Documents… is now the app's, naming the four tabs.

**Decided here, each the web's own:**
- **A tag's document of a volume the catalogue does not list,** which only a Mac's export can bring, one side-loaded there, has no box and is never chosen: S18d's add takes no such volume (`VOLUME_NOT_FOUND`), and one chosen would refuse the whole add. The app's sheet adds it. Its row says why.
- **A note with no document,** a project's, gives the union none, where the app's sheet would list an empty row and add an entry with no ids.
- **Each opening of a tag gathers its documents again,** as the app's `openTag(_:)` does, and keeps no answer for the next opening, nor asks again while it is open, so what is chosen at once is what that opening gathered and showed.
- **A refused Resolve keeps the last lines,** with what was chosen from them, which the reader can still see and unchoose; the app's resolver is never refused.
- **The paste and its lines stay while the sheet is open,** as the app's do; a tag opened goes back to the list when another tab is chosen, as Browse's volume does, where the app's stays open.
- **The hint names the server's index** where the app's names the device's, and the line while it resolves is the web's own, where the app shows a spinner.
- **Add takes 1,000 documents at a time,** S18d's bound, so a tag that gathers more is added in parts; SPEC says so.
- **Kept as the app's:** the drill-in's Tags, which shares its word with the tab's; the tab is a pressed toggle in the group Find documents, so a screen reader tells them apart. And the union reads each note whole (`notes(for:)`), as the Thematic Index's assembly does.

**Tests**

- **FRUSLightCoreTests,** 217 to 218: `UserTagTests` gains `aUsersAssignmentsAreReadInTheOrderTheStoreTookThem`, on each store: an import's later time first, none, a lower-case tag id and a dangling tag in the order the store took them, each user's alone, and a merge re-pointing an assignment where it stands.
- **FRUSLightServerTests,** 302 to 308: `AddDocumentsTests`, 6, two of them on each store:
  - each bucket over the synthetic export, a line pasted twice two rows, and the kit's resolver, built as the app's sheet builds it, answering line for line;
  - the catalogue alone with no index, a link to a chapter finding only its volume;
  - the bounds and the body's refusals;
  - a stopped resolve throwing before its next line;
  - the Tags routes through the router on each store: counts, order, heads, titles, `catalogued`, a project's note, a deleted tag's assignment, another user's tag;
  - the union over each store's rows equal to the kit's over the whole lists, and the project's note the routes leave out.
- **FRUSParityTests,** 232 to 233: `CollectionParityTests` gains `theAddDocumentsCitationsAndTagsAreTheApps`, which holds the app's tabs and their order, its choosing at once and passing over, Resolve's gate, the counts, a row's words, the resolver's construction, the union's inputs and the editor's queries to the app's source, beside the server's calls and the browser app's mirrors; and the word list gains the tabs' nine words, the three lines that count or name, and the editor's footer.
- **The web unit suite,** from 513 tests in 53 files to 528 in 55: `AddDocuments.test.tsx`, 10, and `addDocumentsRules.test.ts`, 5. Each review fix has a test that fails without it, checked by undoing each: the stale answer, the lines kept, the uncatalogued document, one Resolve at a time, and the remembered unchoosing.
- **The browser suite:** `add-documents.spec.ts`, by keyboard alone: a paste of three lines, one resolved and chosen, a best guess for review chosen by Space, one that names a volume only; Add, the focus back on Add Documents…; then a tag on a note and an assignment, its documents chosen as it opens, the focus on Tags, and Add; axe at each step.

**Results**

- **Linux, `swift:6.4-noble`, arm64,** CI's swift job replayed with its PostgreSQL (`scripts/swift --postgres test`), under the heavy lock, over a build folder cloned from S21b's worktree at the pin: 3,250 tests, all passing, where `main` runs 3,242, the row's parameterized tests on app.db and PostgreSQL both; the one skip is the named one, `FTS5StoreTests`' `backupExclusion()`, which Linux's Foundation cannot keep. The build gives no warning.

The browser suite ran 76 specs at the root and 76 under the path, where `main` has 75, `add-documents.spec.ts` among them, and the accounts and sign-in specs. Its first run failed in the new spec alone, whose name for the Search tab also named the Search tab's own Search button; the spec finds each tab in its group now, and the second run, over the same image, passed.

**A cold review,** two subagents given the diff, the row and the app's source, and none of this session's reasoning, one for the server and one for the browser app. What held up is fixed, each with a test where a unit test reaches it:
- **The browser spec would not have run:** a local `opener` shadowed the helper of the same name, which `tsc -b` refuses and which would have stopped the spec after its first Add.

**Records:** this entry and PLAN's S25d paragraph; in SPEC, the web edition's collections paragraph, Add Documents' four tabs, and the collections API's routes. ## Session 20d: administration and jobs

10 November 2026 · branch `claude/awesome-hawking-fa8ad5` · [#113](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/113) · upstream `68bffcf6`, unchanged

Phase 3's round 2 on the server track, the S20 group's last row, beside S25d, and S22b and S23b upstream, on PLAN's defaults, since the owner has not answered the open questions that touch it: accounts made by an admin alone, with no invitation link. Long work runs as a job of a queue that keeps each job in the user store, and an admin follows and stops it, manages the accounts and takes the recovery actions in Administration. SPEC's new section, User data without CloudKit ▸ Jobs and administration, is the whole account of what they do; this entry says what was built where, how it was shown, what the reviews changed, and what S21c and S21d take from it. The branch was cut from `main` at `5604278`, after #110, and the work was kept in local commits until the push.

**Migration 6,** in both dialects: `jobs`, each job's id, a UUID, its `kind`, `subject`, `state`, `progress` and `fraction`, who asked (`requested_by`, NULL for the server), when it was queued, started and finished, its `error`, and who asked it to stop, and when. The store's methods are written once on `RelationalUserStore` (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/UserJobs.swift`), `JobStore`: a job kept whole by an upsert both dialects read (`ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE SET … = excluded.…`), the start's sweep, the newest jobs and the pruning; every write is outside the search mark. The daily backup's rule for a store that holds no research leaves `jobs` out, so that an index's import, the first job, does not hold off the backup of the research after it until the hour.

**The queue** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/JobQueue.swift`), `InProcessJobQueue`, still the process's: one job at a time in the order queued, each a row kept as it goes, its start and end before the next job starts, its progress at most once a second within a line; `InProcessJobQueue.open(store:)` marks every job a stopped server left queued or running failed, in a sentence of its own, before the server's start builds anything that queues one (`ServerComponents.make`). The list is the queue's, the newest 100 finished with the live ones, so it answers while an import holds the store. A job's work takes a `JobContext`: `step(_:fraction:)` checks for a cancel and says what it does, `progress` says it within a step, `checkpoint` checks alone, and `commit` marks the point past which a cancel is refused. A job cancelled while it waits never runs, and `onCancel` tells what waited for it. A job's `error` is a `JobFailure`'s sentence, the server's own, or `Job.unexplained`, with the error in the log.

**The jobs:** the index import (`ImportCoordinator`, `IndexImporter.importExport(at:observer:job:)`), with a checkpoint before each step and its commit before it moves the owner's writing or installs its copy, a cancelled file kept in `/data/import` and settled, `ImportReport.Outcome.cancelled`; the JSON import (`Imports.swift`), in two steps, the file's reading and its one transaction, under the import's own id, its status `IMPORT_CANCELLED` when an admin stopped it; and the index's reset (`ServerState.resetIndex(files:)`).

**The routes** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/AdminJobs.swift`, `AdminUsers.swift`, `AdminStatus.swift`), under `/api/v1/admin`, registered in `AdminRoutes` beside S14b's backup and S20c's keys, behind `/api/v1/me`'s guard and `AdminRoleGuard`, the admin role checked for every route before it runs: status, jobs and a cancel, users with an admin's add, role, disable and password under `local`, a user's research and its erasure, the backups, and the index's reset. An admin's change ends a disabled account's sessions, and an account given a new password, in the store and in what `LocalAccounts` holds of them (`forgetSessions(of:)`), so the change reaches them at once, and a new role at the next request; `AccountStore.changeAccount` refuses a change that would leave no admin who can sign in (`AccountStoreError.lastAdmin`), counted in the change's own transaction. `ResearchErasureStore` (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/UserErasure.swift`) counts a user's rows in the 21 user tables and `secrets`, and erases them, with their search rows and their active project, only while they are what the confirmation named; `ResearchImports` holds off an erasure while that user's import waits or runs, and an import while an erasure runs.

**The browser app** (`web/src/admin/`, `web/src/api/admin.ts`): `/admin`, opening at Status, with Status, Jobs, Users, Backups and Keys as panes laid out as Settings' are, grouped by area for the library's to come, the header's Admin link for an admin on a server that keeps user data, and the words in `copy.ts`'s admin block. The instance's NARA key uses Settings ▸ Keys' `KeySection`, now exported with an `owner`. Every question waits for the request it sends, focus goes back to the button that opened it, and a table wider than its pane scrolls in a region a keyboard can reach.

**The smoke test** gains two steps: `== admin: the import's job`, after the first import, which finds it in the admin's list, finished, asked for by the server; and `== admin: the users, a reader refused, the jobs, and a user's research erased, with local accounts`, after S20b's step and its spec, where erin and frank sign in again, waiting out the slowing that step leaves on the address, frank is refused every route, reads and changes, erin lists the accounts, gives frank a role his session has at once and cannot demote herself, finds the import's job still listed after the three restarts since, and erases frank's research once she has counted it, after which his export is empty and hers is not. With `--e2e`, `web/e2e/admin.spec.ts` walks the five panes by keyboard at the root and under the path, asks and cancels each recovery action, and sets and clears the instance's key.

**How the done-when is shown:**
- An import's job appears, finishes and survives a restart: `jobsRunOneAtATimeAndEachIsARowAsItGoes` and `aJobTheServerStoppedIsMarkedFailedAtTheNextStart` on both stores, `importsAFileOnceItStopsChanging` with the job's kind and file, `theJobsListAndCancel` through the router, and the smoke test's two steps, either side of the restarts between them.
- A job cancelled between steps stops: `aCancelStopsAJobBetweenItsSteps` on both stores, `aCancelBeforeTheFirstStepOrTheCommitStopsTheJobThere`, `anImportCancelledBetweenItsStepsChangesNothing` for the index import, and `theJobsListAndCancel` through the router, a JSON import cancelled while it waits and a job cancelled while it runs.
- An admin erases a user, whose export is then empty while another's is not: `anErasureRemovesOneUsersResearchAlone` and `anErasureIsRefusedOnceTheResearchChanged` on both stores, `anAdminErasesOneUsersResearch` through the router, and the smoke test's step.
- A reader is refused each route: `aReaderIsRefusedEveryRoute`, over every route the admin files register, which `everyRouteTheAdminFilesRegisterIsTested` holds to their source, and the smoke test's step, sixteen routes.
- Playwright by keyboard on Chromium with no axe violations: `web/e2e/admin.spec.ts`, in the smoke test, at the root and under the path.

**Two reviews,** each cold, a subagent given the diff and the row's goals and none of this log: one of the server, asked to weigh the admin role on every route and each route's guard, the erasure's reach on both stores and what it leaves, whether a reset or a disable ends sessions, the last admin, what a job's row carries, and a cancel or the restart's sweep racing a job; one of the browser app, its tests and the smoke test's steps. What held up was fixed before the push:
- **The browser spec would have failed at its first check** (browser): it expected the Status heading to take focus after the header's link, which keeps focus, as every header and pane link does here. The spec now holds the link focused and current, and tabs on into the pane.
- **A session read from the store just before an admin disabled its account, demoted it or set its password could be kept for half a minute** (server), as `forgetSessions` ran between the read and the keeping; and a sign-in kept the role it read before its hash. A session read before any admin's change is no longer kept, and a sign-in takes the role the store holds once its session is kept (`aSignInTakesTheRoleTheStoreHoldsOnceItsSessionIsKept`).
- **The index's reset raced the start's open and the imports** (server): a reset while the start opened the index found there was undone by the open, which then served the removed file; a reset queued behind an index import removed the index that import had just made live, its file gone from the drop zone; and it blanked the readiness of an import queued after it. `ServerState.indexGeneration` now lets a reset win over the start's open, whether the open finishes or fails, and refuses to remove an index made live after the reset was asked for; the route refuses a reset while an index import waits or runs; and the reset leaves a queued import's readiness alone (`aResetRemovesNoIndexMadeLiveAfterItWasAskedFor`). The old index's stack is let go by every route that finds no index, not by one alone.
- **An index import's job, and `/readyz`, could carry the store's own words, which on PostgreSQL may quote a row of the owner's writing, and the server's paths** (server): `ImportProblem.logged` takes them to the log alone.
- **The smoke test's check that erin's research survived frank's erasure could not fail** (browser), since an admin's export counts the instance's corrections too. The step holds erin's own holdings to the same count before and after, and frank's to none, and checks the role it puts back; its first step fails with a line, and polls until the job, not only `/readyz`, has finished.
- **In the panes** (browser): the Erase dialog dropped focus when it counted again, and counted again at every return to the window; a cancel left focus on a button the list then took away, and was not announced; a role was sent at each step through its list; Add an Account took focus back after its request wherever the admin had gone; two buttons' names lacked their visible words; a reading that failed over a list kept polling and said nothing; status lines inserted with their text, or switching role, were not announced; a new password stayed in its fields while it was sent; a browser could offer to save another's password under the admin's own name; and a dialog the browser closed while busy left its state set. The dialog now keeps its Erase, focuses it after a recount and counts once; focus goes to the job's row; a role is chosen, then set with Set Role; focus moves after a request only while it is where the request came from; the names start with the visible words; a failed reading says that what the pane shows may be out of date, stops, and on `ROLE_REQUIRED` asks again who the user is; every pane's status and alert lines are always on the page; the fields are emptied as they are read; a hidden field names whose password it is; and each dialog clears when the browser closes it, keyed by its row. Erasing one's own research also refreshes the app's own copies of it.
- Smaller, all fixed: a cancel asked for while a step then failed was ignored, and the file tried again a minute later; a PostgreSQL database whose default isolation is repeatable read would have let two admins demote each other at once, so every write of the PostgreSQL store now reads committed, a line in S14d's `PostgreSQLUserStore.swift`; an erasure of the store's single user could run beside an index import that brings the owner's writing; two jobs queued at once under one id could both run; the store and the queue forgot different finished jobs; and the progress test's second write was never seen. Before the reviews, the same test had hung on a gate it never opened.
- Left as they are, each the owner's to ask for: Status reads the store's migration and its stored keys' count, so it waits while a JSON import's one transaction writes, where the Jobs pane does not; a job that reaches its end with no step after a cancel was asked for finishes as it would; and two jobs queued at the same moment take the line in the order the store kept their rows.

**Results**

- **Linux, `swift:6.4-noble`, arm64,** CI's swift job replayed with its PostgreSQL (`scripts/swift --postgres test`), under the heavy lock, this package's own targets built clean: 3,265 tests, all passing, the PostgreSQL store's suites among them. Swift Testing's results hold one skip, check 1's Linux skip. FRUSLightCoreTests runs 230 and FRUSLightServerTests 312: the row's suites are `JobQueueTests`, `UserErasureTests` and the coordinator's two in the first, and `AdminRouteTests` and a sign-in's role in the second. The tests that pinned migration 5 (now 6), the store's tables (`jobs` beside `secrets`), the export's tables that are no one's research and the backup's rule for a store that holds none follow this row.
- **The browser app:** typecheck, lint and build pass, and its unit tests, 521 in 54 files, 8 of them this row's (`web/src/admin/Admin.test.tsx`).
- **The image and the smoke test:** `scripts/compose-smoke --e2e` with `frus-light:s20d`, this branch's image, on port 18180, passed every step: its two new ones; 76 browser specs at the root and 76 under the path, the admin spec among them; and the accounts spec and the proxy's sign-in spec after them.

**The group's shared records** (PLAN's rule 5), from the four entries, Sessions 20a, 20b (with its follow-up), 20c and this: SPEC's configuration table (`FRUS_AUTH`'s `local`, `FRUS_TRUSTED_PROXIES` under `local`, `FRUS_ADMIN_USERS`, `FRUS_USER_DATA`'s admin routes, and `FRUS_SECRET_KEY_FILE`'s whole row), its Compose sketch, the tenancy table and the roles, Settings and administration with Settings ▸ Keys and Administration, the user store's migrations 5 and 6, the HTTP API's admin routes, the backups' line on an erasure and the delivery plan's line for the group; the install guide's Administration, its Accounts, its key file, its Settings and its codes; and the README's Status, Known gaps and Next. COORDINATION §5 holds nothing of the group's, which changed no app file and moved no pin, and is left as it is. **The Compose file keeps its key file in the volume:** `compose.yaml` passes no `FRUS_SECRET_KEY_FILE`, so that a Compose install's first start needs no file its operator makes; its key file is apart from every backup, so a backup alone opens no stored key; and a Compose secret, which keeps the key file out of the volume, costs a file made before the first start, without which the server does not start. The install guide shows the secret in `compose.override.yaml`, for a PostgreSQL store, whose servers must share one key file, and for anyone who wants it; SPEC's sketch now says so.

**Left as they are,** each the owner's to ask for: a job's work does not outlive its process, so a job a restart stopped is failed, and its owner queues it again, as an index's import does from its file; several servers sharing a PostgreSQL store would each fail the others' jobs at a start, which phase 6's managed variant claims in the store instead; an erasure reaches no backup, which keeps what the user held until a newer replaces it; and the jobs' rows keep who asked after an erasure, since they hold none of the research.

**Next:** S21c, the library's downloads, migration 7, on the server track once this merges: a download is a job of this queue, as the hand-over note says (`s20d-handover.md`).

## Session 22b: the classifier and one resolution record, upstream

10 November 2026 · branch `claude/s22b-classifier-resolution-record-13dc9b` · [#111](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/111) · upstream `fe9325b2`, unchanged; [FRUS-Explorer#1894](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1894), merged

**Since merged** (S23c's pin move records it): the owner merged FRUS-Explorer#1894 late on 10 November (04:23 UTC on the 11th), directly on S23b's `b70a17bc`, as `40e0cb57`, whose tree is its head's, `7f8f7686`. S23c's pin move, to `4c252c33`, took it and added check 8's comparator to `Package.swift`, as below.

Phase 3's row S22b, of the second upstream batch, after S23b's (FRUS-Explorer#1891, merged first) and before S22c's: Source Explorer's classifier into FRUSCoreKit, and the sequence both Source Explorer views ran in `load()` as one kit value, `SourceExplorerResolution`, which the views draw from and this server will compute alike; and check 8's comparator. The pull request is `claude/source-explorer-resolution-into-kit`, cut from `v2` at `f179c1bd` and rebased before it opened onto `68bffcf6` (FRUS-Explorer#1888 to #1890, documents, a script and a marketing tool, nothing built) and then onto `b70a17bc` (FRUS-Explorer#1891), keeping both pull requests' records in the three files both change. ## Session 25c: Project Home's focus subjects and a lead's line

10 November 2026 · branch `claude/s25c-project-home-focus-subjects-e1e80d` · [#108](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/108) · upstream `fe9325b2`, unchanged

Phase 3's features-track row of wave 2, phase 2's follow-up to S17f, beside S20c, S21b, S22b and S23b, with no upstream pull request, no pin move and no migration: Project Home's focus subjects with their editor, a lead's line under Suggested Next, and a visit's head, each over the kit code FRUS-Explorer#1813 made public at `fb542514`. The row ran across the owner's resumption of 10 November and a stop at the usage limit; the Mac restarted meanwhile, and the session went on, on Opus, from its state note.

**The kit's calls,** compiled from the submodule, none copied:
- `VolumeSubjectProfiles`, decoded from the image's `volume-subject-profiles-index.json`, 380 subjects and 552 volumes' profiles, each ref once, and its `allSubjects`.
- `ProjectFocusSuggestions.suggestions(engagedVolumeIds:profiles:excluding:limit:)`, eight at most, its default, which the app's editor takes.
- `IndexingPipeline.documentSnippets(forKeys:maxLength:)` over the served index, for the leads shown.
- `IndexingPipeline.extractHeader(from:)` and `DocumentDisplayTitle` over a parsed document, with `FRUSDocumentAST.isShapedAsEditorialNote`.

**The server** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/ProjectFocus.swift`, new; `ProjectHome.swift`, `Projects.swift`, `History.swift`, `ServerResources.swift`; one line in `UserData.swift`):
- **The vocabulary** is read the first time a project's page asks, as the app's `VolumeSubjectProfilesStore` reads it: none for a file missing or one that does not decode, and none, the web's own, for one whose vocabulary names a ref twice. The kit's suggestions build `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` by ref, which would trap and stop the server for every user; the generator writes each ref once and the kit's suite fails on a bundled file that repeats one, so this guards a file someone replaced. The reason is kept for the routes' problems.
- **Project Home's answer** gains `focusSubjects`, the vocabulary's subjects the project chose, in the vocabulary's order (`ProjectHomeView.focusSubjectsSection`'s filter), and `focusSuggestions`, the kit's suggestions over the volumes of the documents the project engages, the chosen left out. Both are absent on a server with no vocabulary, where the browser leaves the section out as the app does.
- **The engaged documents** are `ProjectEngagedDocuments.keys(collections:notes:visits:)`, mirrored: the project's notes on a document, the documents read while it was active and its collections' document entries, over the records Project Home's summary already filters to the project, and a key's volume what comes before its first `/`. Not `DocumentEngagementService.gather`, which the coverage tiles take and which counts the highlights of the project's notes as well; the app's editor leaves them out.
- **`GET /api/v1/me/focus-subjects`** is the vocabulary whole, for the editor's All subjects and its search; `SUBJECTS_UNAVAILABLE` (503), with the reason, on a server with none.
- **`PATCH /api/v1/me/projects/{id}`** takes `defaultSubjectTagIds`, the editor's whole list, in the order given and once each. Each ref is the vocabulary's or one the project holds already, as the app's toggle keeps what the project holds, a ref a Mac's export brought that the vocabulary no longer names among them: `SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND` (404) for another, and on a server with no vocabulary `SUBJECTS_UNAVAILABLE` for a ref the project does not hold. A list that changes nothing writes nothing; one in another order, or an import's with a ref twice, is a change and stamps `lastModified`.
- **A lead's line** is the kit's snippet of the served index for the leads shown, read at once by their keys after the rest of Project Home (`ProjectHomeRoutes.withLines`): none while no index is served, none when the read fails, and none for a document the index lacks, as the app's `loadLeadSnippets()` gives none.
- **A visit's head.** A visit to a document the served index does not hold, or any while none is served, is titled as the app's reader titles a document it parsed (`DocumentViewModel.load`): the kit's display title of the head `extractHeader(from:)` reads from the TEI, with the number the document prints, "Editorial Note 2" for a note whose head names nothing. A document with no head and no note's shape takes the reader's label, "Document 1" or a section's title, through `ReadingHistoryTitle`'s rule, as the app records the title the document was opened with; never its bare id. The app's number falls back to the first head that begins with one (`extractDocumentNumber(from:)`, still internal), which a title shows only for a note with no `@n` whose first head names nothing; every shipped document carries `@n`.

**The browser app** (`web/src/research/FocusSubjects.tsx` and `focusSubjectRules.ts`, new; `ProjectHomeScreen.tsx`, `api/research.ts`, `copy.ts`'s `projectHome` block, `styles/app.css`):
- **The section,** between the tiles and the focus tags, as the app orders them: the chosen subjects' chips, Add or Edit, and the app's sentence for none.
- **The editor,** `ProjectFocusSubjectsEditor`'s, a dialog titled Focus Subjects with Done:
  - Focus subjects while the project holds any;
  - Suggested from your volumes while the search field holds nothing at all, with the app's line under it;
  - All subjects under Search subjects: the first fifty while the field, trimmed, is empty, or else each subject whose name, category or subcategory holds the words, whatever their case, or No subjects match.
  - Each row is a checkbox named by the subject, described by "category · subcategory" and "N volumes", saving the whole list.
  - The app's Subjects Unavailable when the server cannot give the vocabulary.
- **A lead's line,** under its context line, to three lines.

**Decided here, each the web's own:**
- **Saves one at a time.** A toggle saves the newest list whole once the save before it is answered, so the server ends with what the rows show. It builds on the newest list made, or else on the server's last answer, which `updateProject` writes into Project Home's cache at once, before the screen draws it.
- **What the rows show.** They show what was made until the server's copy holds it, and the section's chips follow them once the editor has read the vocabulary.
- **A refused save** puts the rows back as the server holds them and reads Project Home again. Why is said in the editor, or under the section once the editor has closed. The editor opens again with no refusal.
- **The focus.** A row that leaves its section hands the focus to the row now in its place, or the last, or the search field from a section gone with its last row. A row that goes any other way while it has the focus hands it to the search field too: one put back after a refusal, or a suggestion the next answer ranks out.
- **For a screen reader,** a status line says each subject added or removed. The editor's title and Done stick above its rows, and the focus reaches a row clear of them (`scroll-padding-top`, WCAG 2.4.11).
- **The summarised lead's difference,** which SPEC now says. A lead the user has summarised shows its opening text, where the Mac shows the summary, since the served copy never holds the index's `summary_text`. An upstream `documentSnippets(forKeys:maxLength:userSource:)` would close it.
- **The web reader's own heading is left.** For a document the index does not hold it is still "Document 3" or a section's title (`DocumentDetail(teiOnly:)`, S12c's), so History and the reader name such a document differently. Moving the reader to the parsed head is a follow-up of its own.

**At both pins.** S21b takes the pin from `fe9325b2` to `v2`, now `68bffcf6`. None of the files this row mirrors or reads changed between the two: `ProjectHomeView.swift`, `ProjectFocusSubjectsEditor.swift`, `ProjectEngagedDocuments.swift`, `VolumeSubjectProfilesStore.swift`, `DocumentViewModel.swift`, the kit's `VolumeSubjectProfiles.swift`, `ProjectFocusSuggestions.swift` and `DocumentDisplayTitle.swift`, and `volume-subject-profiles-index.json` (`git diff --stat fe9325b2 origin/v2`). `FRUSASTNode.swift` changed in its list item, which #1875 gave an id, and not in the line the parity test holds. No file of this row names `DocumentKey`.

They cover the vocabulary and its order, the write and its refusals, a held ref, and a no-op; the editor's suggestions, the kit's over the three volumes the project engages, with each volume the rule leaves out shown to change them; the engaged documents' rule over records with no document; a lead's line over the served index and none without one; and a vocabulary missing, malformed or naming a subject twice leaving the section out while Project Home, a held ref and `/healthz` answer on. `ProjectHistoryTests` has a visit's parsed head over the fixture's preface, d1, d3 and the editorial note d20, served and not, and, new, a note whose head names nothing and a document with no head, with the other user's refusal of a subjects' write.

10 November 2026 · branch `claude/s20c-secrets-keys-ea1af0` · [#109](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/109) · upstream `fe9325b2`, unchanged

The keys the Mac keeps in the Keychain for the outside services it calls, a user's NARA Catalog and Zotero keys and the instance's NARA key, are the server's to keep, sealed, and to use for its own requests alone, from S22e. SPEC's new Stored keys section is the whole account of what they are; this entry says what was built where, how it was shown, what the reviews changed, and what S20d and S22e take from it. The session was stopped by the usage limit and by the Mac's restart at about 13:13, and resumed on Opus; its work was kept in local commits until the push.

**Migration 5,** in both dialects: `secrets`, `user_id` (NULL for the instance's, and a user's rows cascading with the user), `name`, `key_id`, `sealed` and `updated_at`, with two partial unique indexes, one row of a name for each user and one for the instance, which NULL's inequality would otherwise let repeat. The store's methods are written once on `RelationalUserStore` (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/UserSecrets.swift`), `SecretStore`: set, a delete and an insert in one transaction; the sealed row; remove; an owner's names and times; the counts by key file; and `removeSecrets(notSealedUnder:)`. Every write is outside the search mark.

**The key file and the sealing** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/Secrets.swift`): `SecretKey`, the key file's 32 bytes, named by an id HKDF derives from it under a label of its own; `seal` draws a 32-byte salt and a 12-byte nonce from the system's generator for each write, derives the write's key by HKDF-SHA256 with the salt and the secret's binding as its info, and seals with AES-256-GCM, the binding as its additional data; `open` refuses another format, a short row, another key file, another owner or name, and a changed byte. The binding is a label, the owner's kind, the user's id and the name, each length-prefixed, so that no two owners' or names' bindings are the same bytes. `SecretKeyFile` reads a key file, refusing one that is not 32 bytes or not a file, and makes one: written whole to a file of its own with `O_EXCL` at 0600, flushed, then linked under the name, which `link(2)` gives only where nothing has it, so two servers that start together read one key. `SecretVault` is what a route reads and writes through, and `SecretVault.open` the start's rules, each a `SecretKeyProblem` whose sentence the install guide gives word for word, as a test holds it to: a named key file that is missing, one that is not 32 bytes, the server's own gone while the store holds keys, keys sealed under another, and a PostgreSQL store with none named. `ServerComponents.make` opens it after the store (`Application.swift`), and the log names the key file and its id.

**The routes** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/Secrets.swift`): `GET /api/v1/me/secrets`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/v1/me/secrets/{nara|zotero}`, and the same under `/api/v1/admin/secrets` for the instance's `nara`, which needs the admin role, checked before the route reads a body. Both groups are under `UserDataGuard`, `/api/v1/me`'s and the admin group's own lines in `UserData.swift` and `AdminBackup.swift`. No answer carries a key, and a refused key is refused in words that do not repeat it.

**The command line:** `frus-light secrets forget [--all]` (`Sources/FRUSLightServer/SecretCommands.swift`), beside `backup`, `restore` and `user`, for a key file that is lost for good, with the server stopped; and `frus-light restore` says whether the key file in place opens the keys it restored (`StoreCommands.keyFileLine`).

**The backup:** `BackupManifest.secrets`, the table, its rows and the key files' ids, with `keyFileIncluded` false, absent for a backup from before migration 5; `UserStoreRestore.Report.secrets` the same.

**The browser app:** Settings ▸ Keys (`web/src/settings/KeysSettings.tsx`, `web/src/api/secrets.ts`), the pane beside Data under Settings' marker, its route beside Data's, and its words in copy.ts's Settings area, the app's Connections' where they fit: NARA Catalog and Zotero, Key stored and No key stored, each About sentence and link, Add Key…, Replace Key…, Remove Key and its question. The key is typed into a password field, emptied as it is sent, and never kept by the page. The web's own lines say that nothing here uses the keys yet and that whoever runs the server holds the key file.

**The smoke test** gains a step in the settings area, after the import under the path, beside its kin: the keys set through the guard and refused without the token and from another origin, the key file 0600 and the server's, no key as given in the volume, the log or the archive, the archive's manifest listing the table with no key file, a start without the key file refused with the guide's sentence and none made, and a start with it back. Under rule 4 the pull request changes shared files, and this repository changes only its records.

**FRUS-Explorer#1870, in five commits and a records commit:**
- **The corrections check:**
  - `VolumeUpdateChecker`, `hasUpdate(local:live:)`, `LocalVolumeInfo` and `UpdatableVolume` are moved to `FRUSCoreKit/Downloads/`, with `gitBlobSHA1(for:)`. That uses CryptoKit on Apple platforms and swift-crypto here, and `DownloadManager`'s own forwards to it.
  - `updatableVolumes` reads `DownloadedVolumeFiles`, a protocol of the three `DownloadManager` methods it called, which the server's library will conform to.
  - The live listing's entry is now public, `GitHubLiveEntry`, with `volumes(inListing:)`, the fetch's decode and filter (`.xml`, 20,000 bytes or more).
  - `ManifestDiffResult`, `LiveVolumeInfo`, `NewlyAvailableVolume` and the diff, `ManifestDiffResult.diff(bundled:live:)`, are in `FRUSCoreKit/Models/Manifest/ManifestLiveDiff.swift`. `ManifestStore` keeps its fetch.
- **Side-loading:**
  - `SideloadValidator`, `SideloadError` and the root sniffer move out of `SettingsView.swift` into `FRUSCoreKit/Settings/`.
  - `LocalVolumeCatalog` moves into `FRUSCoreKit/Models/Manifest/`.
  - FRUSCoreKit depends on TEIHeaderKit for the catalogue's header read, behind `canImport`.
- **The update review's rules:**
  - `VolumeUpdateReview`'s tallies and `ExcerptReview`'s lines are moved and public.
  - `HighlightReview`'s status is a rule over a highlight's two stored values, `status(renderingVersion:selectedText:currentVersion:)`, in `FRUSCoreKit/DocumentView/HighlightReviewStatus.swift`. The app's `status(of:currentVersion:)` reads its model into it.
- **The indexer:**
  - `consolidatePersonRollup(overrides:forceReload:)` is public.
  - `setStopsBetweenBatchesWhenCancelled(_:)` is new. With it on, a cancelled `indexVolume` throws `CancellationError` after a batch of a volume's documents, as a pass cut short stops (#1566), and `finishIndexing(of:)` stops before its next volume.
  - The row asked for a plain `Task.checkCancellation`. The app cancels one pass, though: the background indexing task iOS expires. A plain check would change how that pass ends, so the stop is a host's choice, off by default and never turned on by the app.
  - On the server a batch is a whole volume, so the check comes once, after a volume's documents and before its other tables.
  - The pull request asks the owner whether the app should turn it on.
- **Two suites moved:**
  - `DocumentRevisionsTests` (28 of its 29 tests in the package; one needs the app's `GeneratedSummary`) and `CorrectedVolumeReindexTests` (2) moved into `FRUSExplorerTests/FRUSCoreKit/`, so Linux runs them.

## Session 25a: PDF through Gotenberg

8 November 2026 · branch `claude/s25a-pdf-gotenberg-1a2861` · [#100](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/100) · upstream `fe9325b2`, unchanged

Phase 3's features-track row of wave 1, beside S20b, S21a and S22a, with no pin move: a collection exports as PDF through Gotenberg's Chromium while the server has the service, and the export sheet offers PDF only while the service answers. The owner has not answered SPEC's question whether a Chromium container is acceptable as the optional PDF path, so PLAN's default, yes, holds; the owner's Gotenberg checkpoint follows.

**The server's PDF service** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/PDFService.swift`, new). `FRUS_PDF_URL`, which the configuration parsed and nothing read, now makes `ServerState.pdf`, the service at that address, http or https, under the path Gotenberg's `--api-root-path` gives it. Each request is one HTTP/1.1 exchange on a connection of its own, through NIO's `ClientBootstrap` and `NIOAsyncChannel`, which FRUSLightCore already links for its PostgreSQL store, with TLS through NIOSSL. FoundationNetworking's URLSession was the other way, and PLAN's choice for the phase's downloads, but its C half, `lib_CFURLSessionInterface.a` in `swift:6.4-noble`, calls libcurl, which the runtime image does not install, and this row adds no package to the image. An exchange sends `Connection: close` and reads the answer whole, by its `Content-Length`, chunked or to the close, 512 MiB at most. A timeout bounds it from the connection to the last byte: three seconds for the health check, and 320 for a print, past the 300 compose.yaml gives Gotenberg. A task cancelled, as when the browser that asked has gone, closes the connection. The health check is Gotenberg's `GET /health`, and its Chromium decides whatever another module says, since the full image reports 503 while LibreOffice alone is down. An answer is kept ten seconds, so the sheet asks the service at most that often, and a print that finds no connection forgets it, so the next ask is fresh. The log says the first answer and each change: "The PDF service at http://pdf:3000 answers: collections export as PDF", or that it does not, and why.

**The routes.** `GET /api/v1/pdf` (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/PDF.swift`, new, its line in `Routes.swift` beside Citation Lookup's) answers `{"available"}`, never cached, outside `/me`, since an analytics figure will need it too. `POST /api/v1/me/collections/{id}/export` takes `pdf`, the app's `ExportFormat` raw value, while the server has a URL. The PDF is the HTML export's page, `CollectionItemHTMLRenderer.pageHTML` over what the assembly resolves for an export with its figures (`printsFigureImages`, as the app's PDF), posted to Gotenberg's `POST /forms/chromium/convert/html` as `index.html`. With it go the app's page from `PDFCollectionExporter`, 612 by 792 points with 72 of margin, sent as 8.5 by 11 inches and 1, and `printBackground`, which a highlight's background needs; Chromium prints the page's own `@media print` rules, Gotenberg's default media. The answer is `application/pdf`, named `CollectionExportNaming.fileName` with `.pdf`, as the app's PDF exporter names its file, and recorded in the history as `pdf`, which History already names PDF. With no URL, `pdf` is no format the server exports, as before (`INVALID_FIELD`). While the service does not answer, the export is `PDF_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (503), asked before the collection is resolved, and so is Gotenberg's own 503, from its time limit or its queue, or a 429. Any other failure, an error of the service's, an answer that is no PDF or one past the limit, is `PDF_NOT_MADE` (502), with the service's first line.

**The export sheet.** `exportFormats` gains `pdf`, first, in the app's order, and `gridFormats(smartCollection, pdf)` keeps it while the server says its service answers. The sheet asks `GET /api/v1/pdf` before it shows its grid, which the editor asks as it opens, so the answer is there and the grid never changes under the reader. With PDF the sheet opens on it, as the app's `ExportSheetView` does (`selectedFormat = .pdf`), and without it on HTML: the grid's first either way. The card is the app's, PDF and Formatted reader. Once the grid shows, the choice it opened on holds, whatever a later answer brings. An export refused as `PDF_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` asks again: where the print found no service, the server has forgotten its answer, so PDF leaves the grid and the sheet falls back to HTML; where Gotenberg was only busy, its 503, PDF stays. The word cloud's note covers PDF too, which draws none, as HTML and Word draw none.

**compose.yaml's `pdf` service.** `gotenberg/gotenberg:8-chromium`, Gotenberg 8 with Chromium alone: 507 MB compressed for amd64 and arm64, where `8`, with LibreOffice, is 697 (Docker Hub, 8 November), and the server uses Chromium's route alone. It stays behind the `pdf` profile, and `FRUS_PDF_URL` stays `http://pdf:3000`, set whether or not the profile runs the service, which the health check now makes harmless. The service is hardened as the server is: read-only, with `/tmp` and Chromium's home, `/home/gotenberg`, each a tmpfs, no capabilities, `no-new-privileges`; and `--chromium-auto-start` starts Chromium with it, so that its health check answers only once Chromium runs (CI's first run, below). It is on a network of its own with the server, which Compose makes internal, so it reaches neither the internet nor the host. Gotenberg's flags give a print 300 seconds, download nothing (`--api-disable-download-from`), run no script (`--chromium-disable-javascript`), fetch no address a page names, private or public (`--chromium-deny-private-ips`, `--chromium-deny-public-ips`), and serve no route but Chromium's (`--pdfengines-disable-routes`, `--webhook-disable`, `--prometheus-disable-collect`). Tried on 8.40.0 with each image: a page naming `https://history.state.gov` and `10.0.0.1` printed, with both addresses refused in Gotenberg's log, and its `data:` image kept.

**The smoke test**, in two steps of a new area, collections, between research's steps and nginx at the root, whose state they need. With the profile off, `/api/v1/pdf` offers none and a collection's PDF is `PDF_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. Then the test starts the profile, once, for the rest of the run, and checks the service is read-only and on the internal network alone. It waits for the server to offer PDF, exports a collection of frus1961-63v06's d1 and d2 as HTML and as PDF, and finds in the PDF's text the titles the HTML export gives the two documents, since the PDF prints that page; the PDF is named `Smoke letters.pdf` and kept in the history. `scripts/pdf-text` (new) reads Chromium's PDFs with Python's standard library, since neither CI's runner nor Gotenberg's image has a PDF reader: the xref table, deflated streams, the page tree, ToUnicode maps of one or two bytes, Tj, TJ, ' and ", and form XObjects. Its selftest, over a PDF it writes with each of those, runs in the step. Matching ignores white space: Chromium starts a text object at each run of a font, as a highlight's `<mark>` is, and a line breaks anywhere a title does. The clean-up names the profile, so the service and its network go too.

**Playwright.** `collection-exports.spec.ts` exports a PDF by keyboard while the server offers it: Export…, the grid's six cards, PDF chosen as the sheet opens, no axe violations, Export PDF by Enter, `Café letters.pdf` beginning `%PDF-`, Export Complete with the focus kept, Escape back to Export…, and History's PDF · 2 documents. It skips where the server offers none. The sheet's other specs hold either way, with `web/e2e/pdf.ts` saying which card the sheet opens on.

**Left as the row has it, and for others:**
- An analytics figure's PDF waits for S24f, as the row says: `GET /api/v1/pdf` is outside `/me` for it, and `PDFService` prints any page.
- The shared parts, for S25b, the group's last row (PLAN rule 5). SPEC's Compose file names `gotenberg/gotenberg:8`, where compose.yaml now runs `8-chromium` with its flags and network. SPEC's configuration table says PDF is hidden when `FRUS_PDF_URL` is unset, which holds, and could add that it is offered only while the service answers. The install guide's Settings table still calls `COMPOSE_PROFILES=pdf` a 700 MB download for PDF export "when it arrives in phase 3"; it is about 500 MB now, and here.
- For S21c, whose downloads PLAN gives to FoundationNetworking: the image needs `libcurl4` first, as above, which rule 4 gives no row after S20b to add; or the downloads take NIO, as this row does.

**Results**

- **Linux, `swift:6.4-noble`, arm64,** `scripts/swift test` under the heavy lock, over a build folder cloned from S20a's worktree at the pin: 2,730 tests, all passing, 12 of them new, `PDFServiceTests` (8) and `PDFExportTests` (4), with the parity suites' new lines. The skips are the Linux backup attribute's and the PostgreSQL store's tests, which need `--postgres`; no store method changed, and CI's swift job runs them.
- **The browser app:** typecheck, lint and build pass, 294 modules where `main` builds 293, the new one `api/pdf.ts`; its unit tests, 480 in 50 files, where `main` has 476: the grid's formats, and the sheet offering PDF first and opening on it, offering none, and dropping it after an export finds no service.
- **The image and the smoke test:** `scripts/compose-smoke --e2e`, with this branch's image as `frus-light:s25a` on port 18130, passed every step. With the profile off the server offered no PDF and refused one; with it, Gotenberg 8.40.0's Chromium printed the collection in 299,941 bytes, which held the two headings the HTML export gives its documents, their citations, "Foreign Relations of the United States, 1961–1963, Volume VI, …, Document 1." and "… Document 2.". The browser suite ran 72 specs at the root and 72 under the path, 71 before, the PDF export by keyboard among them, and the sign-in spec behind the proxy.
- **After CI's first run,** with Chromium started with the service and its home a tmpfs:
  - **Gotenberg's two images** printed with no error from Chromium's start. Gotenberg served nothing until Chromium ran: 1 s on arm64, and 4 s on amd64 under Rosetta. The arm64 service took about 150 MB while idle.
  - **`scripts/compose-smoke --e2e`** passed every step again. The PDF was the same 299,941 bytes, and the browser suite ran 72 specs at the root and 72 under the path, with the sign-in spec.
- **`scripts/pdf-text`:** its selftest, both ways; and Gotenberg's sample prints, titles, ligatures, curly quotes and accented letters read whole.

**Two reviews.**

One in this session, at the code-review skill's high level, raised five points. Three are applied: the install guide promised a print of up to five minutes, where its own nginx recipes wait 60 seconds, and now says to give a long collection's PDF a longer `proxy_read_timeout`; a PDF was held three times over as its answer was read, and is now copied once into its `Data`; and `scripts/pdf-text` took the last bytes `trailer` anywhere for the trailer, and now only after the last object. The route's needing no user is deliberate, as the corpus's routes need none and the analytics will ask it, its probe bounded by the ten seconds; and the sheet's empty grid while the first answer is pending, at most the health check's three seconds, which the editor's early ask makes rare, is left.

A cold review, one subagent given the branch, the row's goals and the project's rules and none of this session's reasoning, found six. The first would have failed CI: the two parity suites export each of `CollectionExportFormat.allCases` from a server with no PDF service, which now begins with `pdf`; they leave PDF out, which has no kit file to hold it to, and `PDFExportTests` holds its page to the HTML export's instead. Then: a `Content-Length` of `-1`, or a chunk's size near `Int.max`, from whatever answered at the address would have trapped the server, and both are refused now, with tests; the sheet's choice could move when its own ask, after the editor's had gone stale, brought another answer, and the choice it opens on now holds; NIO's connect does not stop when its task is cancelled, so the health check's three seconds could be five against an address that drops packets, and the connection is bounded by the exchange's limit too; this entry said a refused PDF always leaves the grid, true only where the print found no service; and the smoke step hid a failed pull's words, which it now shows. The two risks it named, Gotenberg read-only with no capabilities, and its health reporting Chromium up before the first print, the local smoke run passed, and CI's runner then failed on, as below. Before the full run, the session's first filtered run had found one of its own tests that did not compile, a one-line closure the compiler took as throwing nothing.

**CI's first run** failed the smoke test's PDF step, alone, on GitHub's amd64 runner, Ubuntu 24.04 with Docker 28.0.4 and AppArmor: Gotenberg answered the first print 500, a second after the server first found it answering. The failure dump printed the server's log alone, so Gotenberg's reason was not seen, and it could not be made to happen here. Gotenberg 8.40.0's images, with compose.yaml's options, printed the first page after each of 25 fresh starts: the amd64 image's 5 under Rosetta, and the arm64 image's 5 under Docker 28.0.4's seccomp profile and 15 with half a CPU. The whole smoke test passed with the amd64 image as the pdf service. Gotenberg's source and the two images showed what the cold review had named:
- Unless told otherwise, Gotenberg starts Chromium at the first print, and a failed start answers that print 500. Until then its health check calls Chromium up, so a Chromium that could not start was offered.
- Chromium writes to its home, which the read-only root refused. Its crash handler, given no folder, exited at every start (`chrome_crashpad_handler: --database is required`), as in the 500s on a first print that Gotenberg's issues 949 and 966 report from a read-only root; and fontconfig found no cache it could write.

Both are mended in compose.yaml: `--chromium-auto-start`, after which Gotenberg serves nothing until Chromium runs; and `/home/gotenberg` a tmpfs, after which Chromium's start logs neither error. The dump now prints the pdf service's log as well, so that a print Gotenberg refuses says why.

**Records:** this entry; PLAN's S25a paragraph in Where the rows stand; in SPEC, the Collections section's and The user's data's paragraphs for S25a, the API table's PDF row and Deployment's line on the sidecars; and the install guide's PDF export section and its Collections line. README and COORDINATION are left to S25b and the pin moves (rule 5).

## Session 20b, follow-up: the smoke test's session check, in either order of its keys

8 November 2026 · branch `claude/s20b-smoke-key-order-944ee3` · [#104](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/104) · upstream `fe9325b2`, unchanged

`main` went red when #101 merged: its run at `2cbd443` failed in `compose`, at the first check of the smoke test's step for local accounts, which compared `GET /api/v1/auth/session`'s body with the literal `{"auth":"local","signedIn":false}` and was answered `{"signedIn":false,"auth":"local"}`. #101's own run, on the same tree, had passed. PLAN's rule 3 puts the fix on S20b, in a pull request of its own, and holds every other merge, S25a's #100 and S22a's #102 among them, until it is in.

**The cause.** The session's answer goes out, as every answer of the API's but a problem does, through Hummingbird's default encoder, a `JSONEncoder` that sets only its dates; `APIProblem` sorts its keys. swift-foundation's encoder keeps an object's keys in a `Dictionary`, whose order is fixed neither from one process to another nor from one answer to the next: in the build image, three processes that each encoded the session's answer 1,000 times gave 500 of each order in one and `signedIn` first every time in the other two. A check of two keys' order is a coin toss.

**The fix.** The check reads the two fields, as the step's checks of the sign-in's and `/api/v1/me`'s answers already did, and a comment there says why, and when two bodies may be compared whole: when both are problems. The API is left as it is. JSON gives an object's keys no order, SPEC promises none, and nothing reads an answer's bytes, no ETag among them. Sorting the session's keys alone would make one route the exception, and sorting every answer's would cost each large answer a sort for a check's sake.

**The rest of #101, read for the same assumption,** holds none. The smoke test's other checks read fields, and its two comparisons of whole bodies, an unknown name's refusal and a disabled account's each against a wrong password's, compare problems. The Swift tests decode what they check (`AccountBrowser.session()`, `problemCode`). The accounts spec compares parsed values with `toEqual`. The web app's tests parse the bodies they post. No other check in `scripts/compose-smoke` or `web/e2e` compares a body with a literal.

**How it was checked:**
- **`scripts/compose-smoke --e2e`** with `FRUS_IMAGE=frus-light:s20b`, S20b's image, built from the tree `main` has at `2cbd443`, on port 18120: passed, the browser suite's 71 specs at the root and 71 under the path, the accounts spec and the proxy's sign-in spec.
- **The two checks alone,** over four answers: they take the session's answer in both orders, `main`'s failing one among them, and refuse one that is signed in and one that names no local accounts.

**Next:** with `main` green, #100 and #102 merge as rule 3 lets them; S20c, as S20b's entry says.

## Session 20b: local accounts, migration 4

8 November 2026 · branch `claude/s20b-local-accounts-944ee3` · [#101](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/101) · upstream `fe9325b2`, unchanged

Phase 3's wave 1 on the server track, beside S25a, S21a and S22a: SPEC's `FRUS_AUTH=local`, with the owner's defaults, since no other answer came: Argon2id through Ubuntu's `libargon2`, and accounts made by an admin, the first with the command line. SPEC's new Local accounts section is the whole account of what it does; this entry says what was built where, how it was shown, and what the reviews changed.

**The library.** `Sources/CArgon2`, a system library target as `CSQLite` is, whose module map links `argon2` and includes `argon2.h`. `libargon2-dev` gives both: `scripts/swift`, CI's swift job, `upstream-watch.yml`'s watch-kits job and the image's build stage install it, and the runtime stage installs `libargon2-1` (`0~20190702+dfsg-4build1` in noble). `FRUSLightCore` links it; no Mac build does, since `tools/mac-golden` takes `ParityFormat` and `FRUSRichText` alone. `scripts/doctor` checks the header. `scripts/swift`'s derived image is now tagged by its package list (`frus-light-swift:6.4-noble-<cksum>`), so the sessions beside this one, whose checkouts keep the old list until they take `main`, keep their own image rather than rebuilding one shared tag over this one's at each run. Rule 4 names this row as the one that adds a package; the other files the package reaches, `ci.yml`, `upstream-watch.yml`, `scripts/doctor` and `scripts/swift`, change by their install lines and comments alone, outside the paths job and the three jobs' conditions, and `scripts/ci-paths selftest` passes.

**Migration 4,** in both dialects: `users` gains `password_hash`, `role` (`reader` by default, checked to be one of the three; `owner` an admin, as it holds the three roles under `none`), `disabled_at` and `last_sign_in_at`; `sessions` is keyed by the SHA-256 of its cookie's token, with its user (cascading), when it was made, last used and expires. The store methods are written once on `RelationalUserStore` (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/UserAccounts.swift`), `AccountStore` and `SessionStore`, the latter v1 interface 4's, which replaces the in-memory store nothing used; every write is outside the search mark. A user keeps at most 100 sessions. A session is kept only if the account still has the password the sign-in verified and is not disabled. A restore ends every session the backup holds (`UserStoreRestore.endSessions`).

**The server** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/SignIn.swift`): `LocalAccounts`, the hasher, the throttle, two hashing slots with 32 waiting at most, and each session read held for half a minute, as S14e holds a proxy's users, so a request need not wait on an import; `LocalSessionResolver`, the guard's one step under `local`; and `AuthRoutes`, `GET /api/v1/auth/session` in every mode, and under `local` `POST …/sign-in` and `…/sign-out`, under the guard's Host, Origin and body checks, which `UserDataGuard` now gives both as three static checks. `Configuration` accepts `local`, refuses it at an http address that is not this machine, refuses `FRUS_AUTH_HEADER` and `FRUS_ADMIN_USERS` with it, and takes `FRUS_TRUSTED_PROXIES` as the proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For` last address is the browser's. The log says at start how many accounts can sign in, how to make the first, and warns of an https address with no proxy named. `Passwords.swift` is the Argon2id wrapper, at RFC 9106's second recommended option, NFKC first, and the rules for a new password, fifteen characters at least, as NIST SP 800-63B-4 asks of a single factor.

**The command line** (`Sources/FRUSLightServer/UserCommands.swift`): `frus-light user add | set-password | set-role | disable | enable | list`, beside `backup` and `restore`. `enable` and `list` are the row's own additions, the inverse of `disable` and a way to see the accounts before S20d's Users screen. A password is read twice and unseen from a terminal, or once from standard input, and never held while the store is open, so a prompt left unanswered keeps no restore waiting.

**The browser app:** the shell asks `/api/v1/auth/session` first, and with local accounts and no session shows `shell/SignInScreen.tsx` in place of the page asked for, its navigation hidden, asking nothing of a user, so the console stays clean, which the e2e suite holds every spec to; the header names the user with Sign Out; signing in or out forgets every query of a user and what the tab keeps, and moves focus to the new screen's heading; a request refused as `NOT_SIGNED_IN` asks again. `api/auth.ts`, the copy's `signIn` block in the shell's area, and the header's lines in `AppShell.tsx` (the nav takes `hidden` on its own line, so no grouped line moved). The unit tests' `renderAt` seeds the session as a server with no sign-in answers it, unless a test asks for the shell to ask.

**The smoke test** gains a step in the install area, before the proxy's sign-in, beside its kin: the server made again with `FRUS_AUTH=local` under the path, erin and frank made with `frus-light user add` from standard input with a random password, and through curl a session refused, a wrong password and an unknown name refused alike, the cookie's flags and path, erin's tag not frank's, the frame's scripts and figures with no cookie, a disabled account refused as a wrong password is, a sign-out ending the session, `user list`, and the sixth attempt slowed; and with `--e2e`, `web/e2e/accounts.spec.ts` alone (`FRUS_E2E_ACCOUNTS`), which signs erin in and out by keyboard, draws a highlight in the reader's frame, and signs frank in at the same tab to find none of it, with axe at each page. The proxy's step that follows names alice, bob, carol and dave, none of them.

**How the done-when is shown:**
- Two users' data stay apart: `LocalAccountTests.twoUsersResearchStaysApart` and the smoke test's tags; the e2e spec's second user at the same tab.
- A wrong password, an expired session and a disabled account are refused: `aWrongPasswordAnUnknownNameAndNoPasswordAreRefusedAlike` (one verification each, one body), `anExpiredSessionIsRefused` (fourteen days idle, thirty in all), `aDisabledAccountsSessionEndsWithinHalfAMinute`, and the smoke test.
- The fifth failure slows the sixth attempt: `theFifthFailureSlowsTheSixthAttempt`, `attemptsSentAtOnceAreAdmittedOneAfterAnother`, `anAddressThatFailsFiveTimesIsSlowedForEveryName`, and the smoke test's last check.
- A store at migration 3 reaches 4 on both dialects: `aStoreAtMigrationThreeReachesFourOnAppDB` and `PostgreSQLAccountMigrationTests`, with migration 4's columns checked on both in `migrationFourMakesTheAccountsColumnsAndTheSessionsTable`.
- Playwright signs in and out by keyboard on Chromium with no axe violations: `web/e2e/accounts.spec.ts`, in the smoke test.

**Two reviews.** One in this session, at the code-review skill's high level, and one cold, a subagent given the code and the row's goals and none of this log, asked to weigh the hashing, the constant-time refusal, the throttle, the cookie, the session's expiry and the command line. What held up was fixed before the push:
- **Attempts sent at once slipped through the slowing** (cold): the check read the counts, and a failure was counted only after its hash, so thirty-four attempts sent together were all heard. An attempt now counts as a failure from the moment it is admitted, in one step with the check, and a sign-in takes its own back: `attemptsSentAtOnceAreAdmittedOneAfterAnother` sends ten and finds five heard.
- **A sign-in verifying while the command line set a password or disabled the account kept a session** (cold): the store now keeps a session only for the hash that was verified, of an account not disabled (`AccountStoreError.changed`).
- **A disabled account's right password was told apart, and not counted** (cold): it is `SIGN_IN_FAILED` now, as any other refusal, so a guess learns nothing of a password it cannot use.
- **Cookies naming two people's sessions** (cold), as a cookie another site under the host could plant beside the browser's own: such a request now names no one.
- **A restore brought back sessions ended since the backup** (cold): it now ends every session it restores.
- **Eviction could free a slowed count, and an https server with no proxy named counts everyone by the proxy's address** (cold): the counts that slow are the last pruned, and the log warns of the second at start.
- **`X-Forwarded-For` was walked past every trusted address** (high), so a browser inside a trusted range chose its own key: only the last address, the one the proxy appended, is read.
- **The prompt held the server's lock** (high), **the old session ended before the new one was kept** (high), **the sign-in's guard copied the write guard's checks** (high, now `UserDataGuard`'s three static checks, which both call), and **the unit tests' session seeding hung on a module flag** (high, now `renderAt`'s `askSession`).

**Results**

**Left as they are,** each the owner's to ask for: the slowing keyed by a name can keep a known name out, a wait of fifteen minutes at a time, for as long as someone keeps failing for it, as any count by name can, and an IPv6 address counts by its /64, so a holder of a /48 has many; the cookie keeps its path rather than a `__Host-` prefix, which would scope it to the whole host, and a request whose cookies name two people's sessions names no one instead; and `GET /api/v1/admin/backup` carries every account's Argon2id hash, as it carries everything else the store holds, for the admin alone.
