## Session 20a: CI and the files for parallel sessions

8 November 2026 · branch `claude/s20a-ci-parallel-files-0178db` · [#99](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/99) · upstream `fe9325b2`, unchanged

Phase 3's first row, wave 0, alone, begun on the owner's word of 8 November, "start phase 3 plan. auto-merge PRs after CI is green.": CI skips its three jobs for a pull request that changes only the records, the files every page registers in are grouped by area, and the browser libraries phase 3 draws with are in the lockfile. Wave 1 starts once it merges.

**The paths job.** `ci.yml`'s first job, `paths`, runs `scripts/ci-paths`, new: its selftest, then `changed`, which reads the merge commit GitHub makes for a pull request. It checks that the checkout is that commit (`GITHUB_SHA`), that it has two parents, and that the second is the pull request's head (`PR_HEAD`, from the event); then it lists every path the commit changes from its first parent, the base branch's head, with `git diff-tree`, plumbing that no configuration changes: renames off, so a file moved into `docs/` counts by the path it left; submodules not ignored, so a pin move counts; each name NUL-terminated, whatever it holds. It writes `code=false` when every path is a record and `code=true` otherwise, and fails, writing nothing, when it cannot tell. A record is a file under `docs/` but the install guide, or a Markdown file at the root: the plan, the log, the specification, the coordination, the prep notes, the README and `CLAUDE.md`. `docs/INSTALL.md` is no record, since `scripts/compose-smoke` runs its nginx recipes; no job reads another record, and the image copies none. A Markdown file in any other folder, the READMEs under `fixtures/` and `tools/` among them, runs the jobs, since the jobs build and read those folders. `swift`, `web` and `compose` keep their names, the contexts `main`'s protection requires, and each needs `paths`, under one condition:

```yaml
if: ${{ !(needs.paths.result == 'success' && needs.paths.outputs.code == 'false') && (needs.paths.result != 'success' || !cancelled()) }}
```

So they are skipped, which GitHub reports as passed, only when the paths job succeeded and wrote `false`; when it fails, times out or is cancelled, or writes nothing or another word, they run, and the condition reads `cancelled()` only once the paths job has succeeded, since GitHub could read it as true after a job's own timeout, which leaves the job cancelled as a cancelled run does. A condition keyed on `true` would skip them when the job writes nothing, and one with no status function, GitHub's implicit `success()`, would skip them when it fails; either way auto-merge would read the skip as a pass. A step that hangs ends at its own limit, as a failure, and the job's fifteen minutes, which would end it cancelled, are beyond the steps' sum; the three jobs run after either. A run cancelled after the paths job succeeded leaves them cancelled, not skipped. `upstream-watch.yml`'s `watch-report` waits on two jobs under `!cancelled()`, and in that workflow's two cancelled pull request runs of 23 October (39887078147 and 39886183272), cancelled while `watch-kits` ran, GitHub reported it cancelled, with no step run, and so did its check run; in `image.yml`'s cancelled runs of 8 November (42446265633) and 29 October (40809138383), every job still waiting on the build was reported cancelled, `publish` among them, whose own condition would have skipped it. A run cancelled while the paths job runs lets the three run to the end, the cost of not reading `cancelled()` then: two pushes to one branch within the paths job's half-minute run both runs' jobs. The compose job runs the selftest again, so a change that breaks the rules or the conditions fails a check `main` requires.

**What a push to `main` runs:** all three jobs, always. `changed` writes `code=true` for any event but a pull request, before it reads git. `main`'s run is the one that tests what merged together, since no branch must be up to date first; and GitHub's concurrency replaces a run waiting on `main` with the next push's, so after two quick merges, code and then the records, only the second's run may start, and a verdict on its own diff would skip the code the first brought. `image.yml` builds every push to `main`, as before.

**How the failure path was checked,** without a CI run of its own:
- `scripts/ci-paths selftest`: 36 paths against the rules, and 18 verdicts over merge commits it makes as GitHub makes them, the base branch's head first: the records alone skip the jobs, and so do records named with spaces, a UTF-8 letter or a line break, and the records alone merged into a `main` that moved on with code; code, the install guide, the records with code, code moved into `docs/`, code removed, a pin move with the records, a merge commit that changes no path, a push and a run outside Actions run them; a HEAD that is not the run's commit, a HEAD that is no merge commit, a second parent that is not `PR_HEAD`, no `PR_HEAD`, and a clone one commit deep fail, where one two commits deep, as the paths job fetches, reads the parents. Then `ci.yml` itself: the paths job first, with its output, its depth and its two commands; the three jobs' names and `needs`, and one condition among them, evaluated in GitHub's expression syntax over forty outcomes of the paths job (the run cancelled or not; the job succeeded, failed, was cancelled or skipped; its output `false`, `true`, empty, missing or another word). The jobs are skipped in the one outcome, run in every outcome where the paths job did not succeed, whatever `cancelled()` reads, and are started by no run cancelled after it succeeded. The selftest also requires its evaluator to find fault with the condition keyed on `true`, with a form that skips on an empty verdict, and with one that reads `cancelled()` when the paths job did not succeed.
- Seventeen mutations, each in a copy of the script or of `ci.yml`, each failed the selftest at its case: the porcelain `git diff`, which follows a rename; submodules ignored; the install guide a record; no check of the second parent, or of HEAD against `GITHUB_SHA`; an empty diff skipping; no `-z`; a Markdown file anywhere a record; a push judged by its diff; the condition keyed on `true`; the first form of the condition, `!cancelled() && …`, which read `cancelled()` whatever the paths job's result; `always()` for `!cancelled()`; no status function; `fetch-depth: 1`; `compose` without the condition; `web` renamed; the compose job's selftest taken out.
- It passes under macOS's bash 3.2 with Python 3.9, and its git cases under bash 5.2 and git 2.43 in `swift:6.4-noble`, which has no python3, so there the selftest now stops at once and says to run it on the host; GitHub's `ubuntu-24.04` runners have both. `ci.yml` parses as YAML, each condition a string.
- What only GitHub can show: that a pull request whose run skips the three jobs is mergeable, which S21a's records pull request will show. How GitHub reads `cancelled()` after a job's own timeout no longer matters: the condition reads it only once the paths job has succeeded.

**The files every page registers in,** grouped by area under a line each, `// ─── Area ───`, in the order the row names them, browse and search, the reader, research, collections, tools, settings and admin, with the shell first where a file has entries of its own:
- `web/src/router.tsx`: its imports, its routes and its tree. Citation Lookup moves to tools, after collections, and nothing else crosses an area. The router ranks a path by its segments, not by its place in the tree, and `/lookup` ties with no other path.
- `copy.ts`: its fifty blocks, each moved whole with its doc comment, in their old order within an area: the project picker to the shell; All Notes, Project Home, History and the Research page to research, after the rail's blocks; Citation Lookup to tools; and Settings, the tag editor, Merge Tag, Data, Projects, the list order, Research Sessions and Reading to settings. In Node the object it exports is the same before and after, every value and the source of each of its 215 functions, each block's keys in their order; only the blocks' order changed, which nothing reads, since the parity tests find a block by its key.
- `AppShell.tsx`'s header links and `SettingsPanes.tsx`'s panes keep their order, which a reader sees. The header's lines are browse and search, research, collections, tools, settings and admin; the panes' are research (Tags, Projects, Research Sessions), the reader (Reading), tools and settings (Data). A line with nothing under it is a later row's place: admin for S20d's link, tools for S24i's Word Cloud pane, settings for S20c's Keys.
- `scripts/compose-smoke`'s steps name their area, `== area: step`: the install, for the image, Compose, the proxy's recipes, the health checks and the sign-in through the proxy; browse and search, and the reader; research; settings, for the JSON import; admin, for the index's imports and the backups; and all areas, for the browser suite. The steps keep their order, since each needs the state the one before it left, so a row adds its step beside its kin in the phase whose state it needs.
- Each file's head says so, for the session that adds to it. Only comments, blank lines, the smoke test's step lines and the order of whole entries changed: every other line is as it was, as each file's lines before and after compare. `api/types.ts` and `styles/app.css`, which rule 4 also lists, are not this row's files and stay as they are.

**The libraries:** Vega-Lite 6.5.0, vega 6.4.0, its peer, vega-embed 7.3.0 and Cytoscape.js 3.34.4, saved exact as `web/.npmrc` has it, each the latest release and published three weeks or more before, under BSD-3-Clause and MIT. The lockfile adds 87 packages, none with an install script and `canvas` not among them, under MIT, ISC, BSD-3-Clause, 0BSD and the Unlicense; two it held, `@types/estree` and `escalade`, lose their `dev` flag, since the libraries need them too, and no version changes. Nothing imports them: built with them added and nothing else changed, `main`'s browser app is byte for byte the same, all five files of `web/dist`, and this branch builds the same 293 modules as `main`.

**The owner's rule of 8 November:** a session enables GitHub's auto-merge on its own pull request once its row is done, and GitHub merges it when `swift`, `web` and `compose` pass. PLAN's open questions record the answer, and rule 3 of How sessions run beside each other and the Settings, phase 3 checkpoint follow it; upstream pull requests are still the owner's to merge, after the Mac check. When this row began, `main`'s protection required `swift` and `compose`; the owner said yes to `web` the same day and it was made required, as the protection read again before this pull request's last push shows, so auto-merge waits for all three, and PLAN's question on `web` is answered too.

**Results**

- **Linux, `swift:6.4-noble`, arm64,** CI's swift job replayed with its PostgreSQL (`scripts/swift --postgres test`), under the app's lock, this package's own targets built clean over a build folder copied from another worktree at the pin: 2,718 tests, as on `main`, all passing. Swift Testing's results file holds one skip, the Linux-only skip SPEC's check 1 names, and the log no other skip or cancellation, by the swift job's own checks. No Swift file changes; the parity tests that read `copy.ts` find each block by its key.
- **The browser app:** typecheck, lint and build pass, and its unit tests, 476 in 50 files, as on `main`.
- **The image and the smoke test:** `scripts/compose-smoke --e2e`, with this branch's image under a tag and a port of this session's own, passed every step, each named by its area: 71 browser specs at the root and 71 under the path, and the sign-in spec behind the proxy. The image's browser app is this branch's build, its assets under the same hashes.
- **The paths job's selftest:** 55 checks, two seconds on the Mac.

**Two reviews.** One in this session, at the code-review skill's high level, raised three points, applied in the pull request's third commit at the owner's request: the condition read `cancelled()` whatever the paths job's result, so a paths job cancelled by its own timeout rested on GitHub's reading of it, and now reads it only once that job has succeeded; the selftest's evaluator knows only the syntax the conditions use, and `ci.yml`'s comment and the evaluator's errors now name that syntax and say to extend it in the change that needs more; and the selftest needs python3, which `swift:6.4-noble` lacks, and now says so at once. A cold review, one subagent given the code and the row's goals and none of this log, found no correctness bug: it enumerated the paths job's outcomes as the selftest does, found that no job reads a record, the fifty blocks byte for byte the same and the header's and the panes' order kept, and ran the selftest itself. It left two risks. The first, how GitHub reports jobs a cancelled run leaves waiting under `!cancelled()`, `upstream-watch.yml`'s cancelled runs then settled, as above. The second, that a pull request is judged by its own copy of the script, so one that changed the rules and their cases together could skip its own jobs, is left as it is: a pull request that changes the script lists it among its paths, and the selftest holds `scripts/ci-paths` to be no record, so its rules would have to misjudge their own file to skip, and a pull request can edit `ci.yml` anyway. The reviewer's hardening for it, running the base branch's copy of the script as well and skipping only when both say `false`, is the owner's to ask for. Its two nits, this entry's results, written last, and a comment in `ci.yml` on the job's limit, are done.

**Records:** this entry; and in PLAN, S20a's paragraph in Where the rows stand, rule 3, the Settings, phase 3 checkpoint, the open questions, and the two lines that named `main`'s required checks, under Before the first session and in How sessions run beside each other.

## The Add to Collection picker's add, answered after its Cancel

8 November 2026 · branch `claude/agitated-mahavira-8861aa` · [#97](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/97) · upstream `fe9325b2`, unchanged

The session given New Collection's late answer, which #95's review left for a pull request of its own, and the collection specs' cleanup found a third race of the same kind while reading the picker: the picker's own add. The owner chose to carry the first two in [#96](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/96), where they landed with its merge (`406d16e`): New Collection's `useStillOpen` guard, on the Collections list and in the picker, and the specs' cleanup from the Collections list. This pull request carries the picker's add alone, at the owner's word, branched from `main` at #96's merge. It is outside `PLAN.md`'s table, so its entry sits directly above #96's, the one it follows. There is no app behaviour to mirror, since the app's add commits at once: the web's rule is that a dialog cancelled leaves the screen alone. No copy, server file or parity line changes.

**What a late answer did.** A collection pressed in the picker sets the picker's close, after Added's 0.6 s (0.8 s for a document it held), once the server answers. Answered after the picker's Cancel or Escape, that close was set after the picker had gone, past the cleanup that clears it, so nothing cleared it: it closed whatever picker the research rail or the reader had opened since, and sent focus to the rail's Add to Collection or to the reader's frame, and with no picker open it still moved focus there.

**What the web does now.** The picker checks `useStillOpen()`, exported from `CollectionsScreen.tsx` for it, once the add is answered and before it shows a failure, as New Collection's sheet and Rename's and Delete…'s dialogs do. An add answered after Cancel or Escape stays in its collection, and the screen stays as the reader left it. Cancel or Escape during Added's pause was safe already, since the picker's cleanup clears a close set before it.

**Test.** `EditorChanges.test.tsx`, after the picker's add and #96's New Collection test: an add answered after the picker's Cancel, from a rail that opens the picker again, leaves the picker opened since, and its focused Cancel, alone past Added's pause. It fails without the guard, the picker opened since closed. The browser app's unit tests go from 475 to 476.

**Results**

- **The browser app:** `scripts/npm` typecheck, lint and build pass, and its unit tests, 476 in 50 files.
- **The image and the smoke test:** `scripts/compose-smoke --e2e`, with an image of the final tree under a tag and a port of this session's own, passed every step: 71 browser specs at the root and 71 under the path, and the sign-in spec behind the proxy.
- **Linux** was not run again at the final tree: no Swift file changes, and the parity tests' lines in `CollectionPicker.tsx` and `CollectionsScreen.tsx` stand; CI's swift job runs it. Over `6472df1`, before #96 merged, the branch's first form, with New Collection's guard and its tests besides this fix, passed `scripts/swift --postgres`'s 2,692 tests with only the named skip, the web's suites, the smoke test with 69 specs in each pass, and `collections.spec.ts` alone five times over at the root.

**A cold review,** one subagent given the code and none of this log, over the branch's first form, found no defect: its mutation runs, each guard taken out of a copy, failed exactly the tests written for it. It noted one behaviour older than this change and outside its rule, since no Cancel is pressed: the picker's close after an add also takes a New Collection sheet opened inside the picker meanwhile. The app's picker closes itself after the same pause, its New Collection offered throughout (`CollectionPickerSheet.swift`), so it is left as it is.

**Records:** none but this entry. `README.md` is untouched: its Known gaps never named this race.

**Next:** the two follow-ups the move to `fb542514` unblocked (Project Home's focus subjects, their editor, a lead's line and a visit's head; Add Documents' Citations and Tags), each a pull request of its own; S20a.

## Pin move to `fe9325b2`, follow-up: the editors' annotations on a volume's page and in Browse

7 November 2026 · branch `claude/admiring-solomon-97acee` · [#96](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/96) · upstream `fe9325b2`, unchanged

The pin move to `fe9325b2` ([#94](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/94)) brought the app's editors' annotations (FRUS-Explorer#1859 to #1862) and showed none of them: a bundled `volume-annotations-index.json`, which the image already carries with the app's other data files, the kit's `VolumeAnnotations` and `VolumeAnnotationsIndex`, and two surfaces of the app's, "Editors’ Annotations" on every volume's page and an axis of that name in Browse. This follow-up, outside the plan's table, shows both as the app does. It was branched from `main` at the move's merge, and its entry sits above the move's and above the collections list's follow-up's, which merged first.

**Where the logic lives.** The rules are the kit's, and the server calls them over the bundled file: when a volume carries a category (half its documents, a tenth or any one: `VolumeAnnotations.carries(_:)`, `carriesSourceNotes`), its era (`AnnotationEra`), and the era from which the series made a practice standard, the first band from which every later band has three quarters of its volumes carrying it (`VolumeAnnotationsIndex.onset(where:)`). What the app builds over them is its view code, in three Foundation-only files: the table of fifteen layers, each a category or several taken together (`AnnotationLayer`), a layer's reach and its lists (`AnnotationsAxis`), and a volume's rows and absent layers (`VolumeAnnotationsPresentation`). Without their words and comments it is a few hundred lines of grouping, ordering and choosing which count a line says, small and view-like, so it is mirrored, as PLAN's rule for view code has it, and held by a parity test that reads the app's source at the pin; no upstream pull request was needed. The server's half is the structure, so the reaches across 553 volumes and the lists are computed once, beside the kit; the browser app's half is the words.

**The server** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/Annotations.swift`, and a line each in `Routes.swift` and `ServerResources.swift`):
- **The file** is decoded once, on first use, by the kit's `VolumeAnnotationsIndex`, as the app's `VolumeAnnotationsStore.shared` decodes it, with each layer's reach computed then. A file missing, malformed or holding no volume, which the app's axis shows as unavailable too, is no reason not to start, and every route answers it with `ANNOTATIONS_UNAVAILABLE` (503).
- **`GET /api/v1/volumes/{v}/annotations`:** a volume's section, for any catalogue volume the file holds, with no index needed: the groups that hold a row, each row its layer and its line as parts (`ofDocuments` with its two counts, `personsListed`, `documents`, `sourceForm`, `aid` and the rest), and the standard layers it lacks with the era each became standard in.
- **`GET /api/v1/annotations`:** the axis, each layer's reach, its eras' bands, and its onset or, for a practice no era made standard, the era where it is most common, ties to the earlier, as `standardLine(for:)` chooses. **`/annotations/{layer}`:** a layer's page and its lists' counts. **`/annotations/{layer}/drills/{drill}`:** a list, with `from`, the volume whose page opened the layer's, first. **`/annotations/{layer}/eras/{era}`:** a cell's list. Each volume of a list carries its count as the app's accessory says it (a ratio, notes or documents) and its marks: the list it prints that nothing links to, and that the reader came from it.

**The browser app** (`web/src/browse/VolumeAnnotations.tsx`, `AnnotationsScreen.tsx`, `annotationRules.ts`, `web/src/api/annotations.ts`, the `annotations` block of `copy.ts`, and a line or a few each in `VolumeScreen.tsx`, `router.tsx`, `Breadcrumb.tsx`, `BrowseAxes.tsx` and `app.css`):

The axis draws each group as the app's regular-width matrix: the eras' first years over eleven columns, each layer's row its name and how many volumes carry it, read aloud with when it became standard, and a cell per era shaded by the share of its volumes that carry the layer, which opens them; a cell no volume of its era fills is drawn, read and disabled. A table with headers suits a matrix in a browser, and it scrolls across at a phone's width rather than falling back to the iPhone's strip.
- **A layer's page** says how many volumes carry it and by what rule, what the editors did, when it became standard, its eras with each one's count read aloud, what the app does with it, and its lists, which open the volumes by the catalogue's titles with each one's count and its amber line. - **The current page, marked once.** The router marks a link the current page wherever the path goes on below it, so All Volumes was marked current on every other axis, and every crumb on the way to a page. `BrowseAxes` and `Breadcrumb` mark a link current on its own path alone, as the Research page's nav does, which mends Working Corpora's, My Scopes', a volume's and a section's pages as well.

The web's own: four "In the app" sentences, whose screens this server does not have yet (people: the reader's card where the app names the People browser and Person analytics; source notes, the reader where it names Source Explorer and the Archives axis; classification, the reader, which prints the marking as the volume does, where it names Search's rows and Source Explorer; cross-references, the reader alone, without the graph); despatch numbers take the app's sentence for a layer nothing else reads, since it names Source Explorer; and a server that cannot read the file keeps the first sentence of the app's line, which goes on to say to reinstall the app.

## Pin move to `fe9325b2`, follow-up: the Collections list's Rename, and its question before a delete

7 November 2026 · branch `claude/sleepy-bartik-7f0fbf` · [#95](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/95) · upstream `fe9325b2`, unchanged

The pin move left the app's [#1831](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1831) for a pull request of its own: both of the app's Collections managers rename, duplicate and delete a collection, and every delete asks first. The web's list had Duplicate, Create Static Snapshot and a Delete… that asked in the web's own words, and no Rename. This follows the iPhone and iPad list, `CollectionListView`, which the Collections tab mirrors; the Mac's Collection menu and Manage Collections sheet have no counterpart here. It is outside `PLAN.md`'s table, so its entry sits above the one it follows. No upstream change, no pin move.

**What the app's list does since #1831,** at `fe9325b2`, unchanged since by any later commit:
- A row's menu offers Rename, Duplicate, Word Cloud, Create Static Snapshot for a smart collection, then Delete.
- Rename presents the Rename Collection alert (`collectionRenameAlert`): a field holding the name as saved, its placeholder Collection Name, then Cancel and Save. Save commits through `CollectionEditorCommit.rename`, the editor's `name` except that a name left empty keeps the old one, and saves. It does not call the editor's `recordEdit()`, so the collection stays in the projects it was in.
- Every delete asks first (`collectionDeleteConfirmation`), in `CollectionDeletion`'s words: its title, Delete “Cold War Readers”? for one, named as its row prints it, and Delete 3 collections? for several; its message; and Delete and Cancel. The swipe, the menu and Edit's Delete of several rows all ask.

**What the web does now**
- **Rename,** first on each row. The alert is a dialog: its field holds the name as saved and takes focus, Escape is its Cancel and Enter its Save, and Save takes an empty name, as the alert's does, where New Collection's Create waits for one. Focus comes back to the row's Rename, wherever the renamed row now sits. Save on the name as it opened sends nothing, as the alert writes nothing for it, which also keeps a rename made in another window after the list was read from being undone.
- **The server's route,** `POST /api/v1/me/collections/{id}/rename` with `{"name"}`, commits it by `CollectionEditing.rename`, over `CollectionEditing.name`, the editor's commit, which `PATCH` now calls too. `PATCH`'s name could not serve: it writes an empty name as empty, as the editor's Name does, and it files the collection under the project the user works in, as the editor's `recordEdit()` does, which the app's Rename never does. The route is `changed(_:for:in:at:_:)`'s one write, which stamps the collection only where the name changed, so the list then reads it first. It takes `PATCH`'s body limit, so a name with U+0000 or past a note's limit, any other field, and another user's collection are refused as `PATCH` refuses them.
- **Delete…** asks the app's question for the one collection a row deletes: Delete “Berlin”?, the app's message, then Cancel, which takes focus, and Delete. The button stays the web's own Delete…, as All Notes' rows have one for the app's menu item. The web deletes one collection at a time, so the app's title and message for several are not taken.
- **Left out:** the menu's Word Cloud, until the web has a word cloud (S24i); and Edit's choice of several rows, which the web's list has never had.

**Held to the app's source.** `CollectionParityTests` gains, beside its lines for the list:
- in `theAppsWordsAreTheWebs`, Rename, the alert's title, placeholder, Cancel and Save, and the question's title, message, Delete and Cancel, each under its key and in copy.ts's `collections` block;
- in `theServersMirrorsAreTheApps`, the app's `name` and `rename`, and the alert's Save, which saves what `rename` commits and no more; that the alert never reaches the editor's `recordEdit()`, nor any project of the collection's; the server's `CollectionEditing` lines beside them; and the mirror's answers for an empty name, the same name and a new one;
- in `theWebsMirrorsAreTheApps`, the menu's order, Word Cloud's place in it, the question every delete asks and the name its title gives; and the web's row in the menu's order, the alert's field holding the name as saved, and the question named by the row.

`CollectionFileParityTests`' line for Create Static Snapshot, which the pin move updated for #1831, stands.

**Tests**
- **The server:** `CollectionTests.aRenameIsTheListsAlert`, over two collections stamped alike, which the list orders as the store took them. An empty name, one of spaces and the same name padded each keep the second's name and write nothing, so its stamp and its place stand. A new name is trimmed and stamped, which lists it first, and leaves the collection out of the project the user works in, where the editor's Name, sent next, files it there. No name, a null one, another field and an unknown collection are refused. The refusal and isolation tests take the route too: U+0000 in its name, a name past a note's limit, and another user's collection.
- **The browser app's unit tests:** the row's buttons in the menu's order; the alert's field, focused and holding the saved name; a rename sent as typed and its row first under its new name, focus back on its Rename; Cancel, and Save on the name as it opened, which send nothing; an empty name, which Save sends and the server keeps; Delete…'s question in the app's words, Cancel then Delete; and a rename or a delete answered after its dialog's Cancel, which leaves the dialog opened since, and its focus, alone. Those two fail with the dialogs as they were. The web app's unit tests go from 455 to 459.
- **Playwright,** in `collections.spec.ts`'s keyboard test, from the list: Rename's alert, focused on its field holding the name, with no axe violations; Escape, then an empty name, each leaving the name and returning focus to the row's Rename; then a new name, the row first under it; and Delete…'s question for it, by its new name and in the app's words, with no axe violations. Its pointer test renames the duplicate before deleting it. The browser suite keeps its 69 tests in each pass.

**Narrow widths.** In the in-app browser at a phone's 375 px, a smart collection's four buttons overflowed its row, and a plain row's three squeezed its name to a word a line. Below 900 px a row's buttons now wrap under its name and caption, as the editor's panes stack below 900 px (`app.css`).

**A cold review,** one subagent given the code and none of this log, found four defects, fixed before the first push:
- **A late answer after Cancel:** Cancel or Escape while a rename or a delete was being answered closed the dialog, but the answer, when it came, closed any dialog opened since and sent focus back to the closed dialog's row. Rename's alert and Delete…'s question now leave the screen as the reader left it once they are closed. New Collection's sheet has the same pattern, older than this change and left for a pull request of its own.
- **The body limit:** the route took a change's 64 KiB, where `PATCH` takes a note's 4 MiB, so a long name the editor's Name keeps could not be sent back. It now takes `PATCH`'s.
- **A vacuous assertion:** the server test's list order held without the rename's stamp, since the collection renamed was already first. It now renames the second.
- **A stale field:** a list read before a rename in another window seeded the field with the old name, which Save wrote back. Save on the name as it opened now sends nothing.

**Results**

- **Linux, `swift:6.4-noble`, arm64,** CI's swift job replayed with its PostgreSQL (`scripts/swift --postgres`) at `fe9325b2`, over `main` at `ec4b881`, under the app's lock, at the final tree: 2,692 tests, against `main`'s 2,691, all passing with only the named skip, in Swift Testing's results file. FRUSLightServerTests runs 242, from 241; FRUSParityTests' 224 hold the new lines in their tests; every other target as on `main`.
- **The browser app:** `scripts/npm` typecheck, lint and build pass, and its unit tests, 459 in 48 files.
- **The image and the smoke test:** `scripts/compose-smoke --e2e`, with an image of the final tree under a tag and a port of this session's own, passed every step, its labels naming build 1787 and index version 74: the browser suite on Chromium passed its 69 tests at the root and 69 under the path, and the sign-in spec behind the proxy. It had passed the same way twice before the review's fixes, and `collections.spec.ts` alone five times over at the root.
- **By eye,** this branch's image in the in-app browser at 800 px and at 375 px, before the review's fixes: the rows, the alert, the question, an empty name keeping the old one, and a rename bringing its row first, with focus on its Rename.

**Records:** `SPEC.md`'s Collections tab line and its API line. `README.md`'s Known gaps still names #1831 among what the web does not show, as the pin move wrote it; under `PLAN.md`'s arrangement the README is the pin moves' and each group's last row's, so the next of them writes it.

**Next:** the pin move's other follow-ups, each a pull request of its own: the editors' annotations; Project Home's focus subjects, their editor, a lead's line and a visit's head; and Add Documents' Citations and Tags. Then S20a.

## Pin move to `fe9325b2`: the app past phase 2, at index version 74

7 November 2026 · branch `claude/upstream-catchup-phase-2-ec6310` · [#94](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/94) · upstream `fe9325b2`

The owner asked to catch up with the app, which had moved on since phase 2's sign-off. The pin moves from `fb542514` to `fe9325b2`, `v2`'s head, in a pull request of its own under rule 5, before any row of phase 3 starts: no row of `PLAN.md` is this move, so its entry sits above the one it follows. The daily watch's issue, [#81](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/issues/81), had reported since 3 November that `v2` was past the pin, at index version 74, and that this package no longer built there.

**What the move brought,** the app's 49 commits from 29 October to 6 November, none of them this project's:
- **Index versions 72 to 74** (#1853, #1857, #1863): the classification marking a 1932–1954 document prints in its opener is stored in `document_sources.classification`, a column the schema already had; SourceNoteKit's parser reads a source note's marking past its second sentence (`classificationMarking(fromSourceNote:)`, and `classificationMarking(fromOpenerLines:)` for the opener); a search row carries the stored one, the kit's public `IndexedSearchRow.classification`, and the app's chip takes the note's marking, else that one, by the kit's `IndexingPipeline.classificationMarking(sourceNote:stored:)`, internal at this pin; frus1941-43's Index of Persons is read as an index, and frus1981-88v16's document-level terms count. The build in `project.yml` is 1787, as at `build-52` (#1837, #1838), the second TestFlight build, which indexes at 71: the app's plan carries version 74 in its next release (its decision 117).
- **The editors' annotations** (#1852, #1855, #1858 to #1862): a bundled `volume-annotations-index.json` of what each volume's editors annotated, its generator, and the kit's `VolumeAnnotations` and `VolumeAnnotationsIndex`, which the app shows on a volume's page and as an axis in Browse.

**What broke, and the repairs.** The package did not build at `v2`: `CollectionContentSource`, the server's data source for a collection's assembly, and the parity harness's `KitSource` answered `generateSummaries` with text, so both now answer with the stored record, as the app's resolver does. `Compatibility.swift` serves index version 74; `SummarizerTests` names build 1787. `Package.swift` compiles the kit by folder, so the new `VolumeAnnotations.swift` needed nothing, and upstream's new generator targets are not compiled here. `tools/mac-golden`'s digest list stands: `project.yml` gained no source folder.

## Phase 3's plan: the library, the archives and local accounts, and how sessions run beside each other

29 October 2026 · branch `claude/phase-3-concurrency-ci-plan-d279ac` · [#93](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/93) · upstream `fb542514`, unchanged

The owner asked for phase 3 to be planned in rows sized one pull request each, as phase 2's were on 23 October, and for the plan to balance how many sessions run at once against the tokens and the CI runs that rebasing parallel pull requests cost, so that they merge one after another. This session changes records only: nothing under `web/`, `Sources/`, `fixtures/` or `.github/`.

**What phase 2 cost,** read on 29 October from the repository and from GitHub:

- **40 pull requests,** #51 to #92, merged between 24 and 29 October, all by the owner.
- **129 CI runs on pull requests:** 41 cancelled by a later push to the same branch, 5 failed, 83 served, about two a pull request; a run takes about twenty minutes, the swift job sixteen and the compose job ten, side by side. `main` ran 52 times, 3 of them red.
- **Forty-one merges of `main` into twenty-three of the forty branches,** to resolve a conflict or to take a change another row had merged; the files they combined were `docs/DEVLOG.md` in nearly every one, and COORDINATION §5's list, the README's Status, `UserData.swift`, `Routes.swift`, `Application.swift`, `router.tsx`, `copy.ts` and `app.css`. One branch (#73) merged `main` six times and ran CI eight; another (#71) five times and six.
- **The files most changed:** the log by 95 commits, COORDINATION 41, SPEC 40, PLAN 36, INSTALL 31, README 30, `copy.ts` 20, `app.css` 19, `UserData.swift` 19, `api/userData.ts` 15, `api/types.ts` 14, `compose-smoke` 13.
- **`main`'s protection** requires `swift` and `compose`, not `web`, and does not require a branch to be up to date, so a green pull request whose files `main` has not touched merges as it is.

**Tested, with `git merge`** in a scratch repository: two branches that each insert an entry at the top of a file conflict; two that each replace a stub of their own merge clean in either order, with one blank line between the stubs and whatever each writes into its own; two that append after the same paragraph, or edit adjacent rows of a table, conflict; one that inserts directly above a stub while another fills it conflicts, so a follow-up's entry goes above its row's entry only once that has merged. GitHub's documentation confirms that a required check whose job is skipped by its own `if` reports success, where a workflow skipped by a path filter stays pending and blocks the merge: S20a's shape.

**Checked against the app's code at the pin** (`docs/prep/README.md`, Phase 3), by four read-only surveys, each claim then read again here:

- **The indexer is the kit's and the web drives it already:** `indexVolume`, `indexAllVolumes`, the progress streams with `IndexingStage.failed`, `removeVolume`, `vacuumIndex`, the revision table and its review calls, and `HighlightReanchor` are public, and `Tests/FRUSParity/ParityIndex.swift` indexes the fixtures on Linux with an in-memory stamp store. Downloads, the corrections check, the sideload validator, the review sheet and the recovery ladder are app code; the served index is opened immutable, which cannot see a write in progress.
- **Source Explorer's resolvers are about 4,200 lines of Foundation-only app code,** internal and loaded through `Bundle.main`, with no view model: a 3,193-line SwiftUI view runs the resolution; SourceNoteKit is a grammar. `NARACatalogClient` (935 lines) and `ZoteroAPIClient` (236) are Foundation-only app actors; check 8's comparator, `SourceExplorerExportGeneratorCore`, is Linux-capable and not compiled here.
- **Related Documents is 4,500 lines of app code over a pure ranker,** every generator and scorer taking `AppState`, with the kit calls they need public; the graph's data is `CrossReferenceStore`, a public app actor over the index's `cross_references`, and a 2,070-line view model holds the layouts.
- **Analytics:** the person store's queries are the kit's and public; Corpus Analytics' service, the cross-reference stats and PageRank, the archival derivations, Chronology's grouping over two internal queries, About the Series' four readers and the CSV method block are about 12,000 lines of app code, Foundation-only but one caption measure and one colour. WordCloudKit imports NaturalLanguage unguarded, so none of it compiles on Linux.
- **The server:** `Configuration` already names `local` and `standalone` and refuses them; the session and job types exist and nothing uses them, the job queue is in memory, serial and without a route; no Argon2 is in the dependency tree, while swift-crypto's extras offer scrypt; the `pdf` profile with Gotenberg 8 is already in `compose.yaml`, and `FRUS_PDF_URL` is parsed and read by nothing.

**The plan** (`PLAN.md`, Phase 3) has 32 rows in six groups, on three tracks:

- **S20, accounts, secrets and administration (server):** CI and the files for parallel sessions (S20a), local accounts with migration 4 (S20b), the secrets table and Settings ▸ Keys (S20c), administration and jobs (S20d).
- **S21, the library:** the library's rules upstream (S21a), the first pin move (S21b), the downloads (S21c), indexing on the server (S21d), sideload, remove, compact and the upgrade (S21e), the corrections check and the update review (S21f), corrections on the web and the People screen (S21g).
- **S22, Source Explorer and the archives:** three upstream pull requests (S22a, S22b, S22c), then Source Explorer with check 8 (S22d) and NARA, Look Up and Zotero (S22e).
- **S23, Related Documents and the graph:** two upstream pull requests (S23a, S23b), the second pin move (S23c), Related Documents with Suggested Next (S23d) and the graph (S23e).
- **S24, analytics, About the Series and the Word Cloud:** four upstream pull requests (S24a to S24d), the third pin move (S24e), and four feature rows (S24f to S24i).
- **S25:** PDF through Gotenberg (S25a) and the sign-off (S25b).

Ten upstream pull requests in three batches, three pin moves, fifteen owner checkpoints, seven risks, the decisions and eight open questions. The arrangement, How sessions run beside each other, has eight rules and a table of waves: four sessions at once on three tracks, a branch merged from `main` only on a reported conflict, the owner's merge sitting in the table's order, each row's files its own with one line a row in the registration files, the records written into stubs and by each group's last row, one CI run a pull request, what a session reads, and upstream batches of three. Its measure: at most two runs a pull request on average, and merges of `main` only where GitHub reported a conflict.

**Records**

- **`PLAN.md`:** the Phase 3 section, with its flowchart, the rows, the arrangement, the waves and a stub for each row's done paragraph; the Summary's line on where the plan stands; the session plan's line on phase 3; rule 8 in the list the first session took; eight owner checkpoints and the golden-files row; seven risks; and the two answer sections.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** rule 8, the arrangement in four clauses.
- **`docs/DEVLOG.md`:** the intro's line on the stubs, and a stub for each row above this entry, in the order the plan expects them to end.
- **`docs/prep/README.md`:** the Phase 3 section, the surveys' claims with file and line.
- **`docs/COORDINATION.md` §5:** phase 3's ten moves into the kit, in the list of app changes.
- **`docs/SPEC.md`:** the delivery plan's progress line. **`README.md`:** the status's Next and the development plan's phase-3 row.

**Results**

- No code changed. CI runs as on any pull request, at the pin.

**Next: S20a,** CI and the files for parallel sessions, alone, since every later records-only pull request depends on it. Then wave 1: S20b and S25a here, and S21a and S22a upstream.

## Session 18f: `.fruscollection` both ways, smart collections and headnotes

29 October 2026 · branch `claude/upbeat-nash-1f07ea` · [#90](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/90) · upstream `32e295e5`, unchanged

Phase 2's row S18f, the last of the collection rows. A collection's `.fruscollection` file is written by the kit's writer and read by its reader: Export… saves one, its prose the RTF the store keeps, with the reader's notes only when they are included, and Import Collection… makes a collection of one, with the notes it brings. A collection linked to a saved search from Collection settings is a smart collection, whose documents are the search's results in the preview and in each export, and Create Static Snapshot freezes them; its entries from before the link are listed apart, to be removed. Summary only is refused with the app's reason where a document has no summary stored, and the inspector's headnote card writes the researcher's headnote and shows an imported one with its authorship. Every file, and every export and preview of a smart collection, is the kit's to the byte. No upstream pull request, no pin move and no schema change: everything the row calls was public at `32e295e5`, since #1809.

**What the kit gives,** at `32e295e5`, since #1809:
- `NativeCollectionSerializer`: `makeFile(from:includeNotes:resolveNoteTexts:)` over a `CollectionExport`, `encode`, `decode` under the tolerant-reader rule, and `importedValues(from:)` into a `NativeCollectionImport`, with `NativeCollectionError`'s sentences.
- `SmartCollectionSnapshot`: `documentRefs(parameters:searchService:limit:)` at `resultLimit`, 1,000, and `snapshot(of:results:)`.
- `CollectionContentAssembly`'s smart path: `resolve(smartRefs:introduction:purpose:fullRefs:)`, and `smartDocumentRefs()` asked of the data source for a full resolve; `CollectionResolveError`'s sentences.

**Delivered**

- **The file** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/CollectionFiles.swift`):
  - the export's fifth format, `fruscollection`, `application/json`, named as `writeTemporaryFile(_:)` names it: the kit's file of the collection's values, a pre-RTF prose blob healed first, and with `includeNotes` each document entry's notes as the sheet's `resolveNoteTexts` gives them; refused for a smart collection in the app's words; kept in the history with its document entries;
  - `POST /api/v1/me/collections/import`, in a route group of its own, 16 MiB, 5,000 entries and 5,000 notes at most: the kit's `decode` and `importedValues(from:)`, off the cooperative pool, each text and id held to what an editor keeps, filed under the project worked in; the collection, its entries and the notes it carries in one write, which rewrites their documents' rows of `user_search`; a headnote draft of the user's an entry names copied for it.
- **Smart collections:**
  - `CollectionSmartSearch` (`CollectionContent.swift`): the saved search's parameters as stored, through the user's search over the served index, at the kit's `resultLimit`, the kit's sentences when no index is served or the search is gone; the routes run it before the resolve and give the data source the results, so each volume is read once;

## Session 18d: collections and their editor

28 October 2026 · branch `claude/inspiring-volhard-81ec2e` · [#86](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/86) · upstream `32e295e5`, unchanged

Phase 2's row S18d, the first of the collection rows S18c's pin move opened. The Collections tab lists the user's collections and makes, duplicates and deletes them; the editor builds one as the app's does, sections three deep, documents, note blocks in S15d's rich text, excerpts frozen from the reader's selection or a highlight, and the five apparatus blocks, with the per-document inspector, a section's defaults, the presets and the order by date; the reader's selection bar has Excerpt, and the Research rail its Collections section. Each rule is the kit's code where #1807 and #1809 moved it there, and app code mirrored, held to the app's source, where it is the editor's. No upstream pull request, no pin move and no schema change: the rows are migration 2's, written as the import writes a Mac's record and read as the export reads one, so a collection made here travels in the JSON export as the Mac's does. One part of the row waits: Add Documents' Citations and Tags, which read kit code kept internal, so they need an upstream pull request first.

**What the kit gives,** at `32e295e5`, from FRUS-Explorer#1807 and #1809:
- `CollectionOutline`: a heading's resolved depth, its section's range, a move's new order and a section's overrides, three levels at most.
- `CollectionPreset` with its `recipe` and `apparatusBlocks(notAlreadyIn:)`; `CollectionBodyDepth.available(summariesAvailable:)` and `resolve`; `CollectionFootnoteStyle`'s flags.
- `CollectionGeneratedBlockType` with its `defaultPosition`, the chronology at the front; `CollectionEntryKind`, with `unrecognized` for an entry a newer build wrote.
- `CollectionEditorNaming`: a row's name, the list's order and the untitled section.
- And from earlier pins: `flatTextExcerpt` and `renderingVersion(for:)` for an excerpt of the page, and `HistoryAtStateCitationFormatter` for the inspector's derived title.

**Delivered**

- **The store** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/UserCollections.swift`): `CollectionStore` over migration 2's `collections` and `collection_entries`, on both stores: a collection read and made with its entries; changed in one write that reads them, asks the API what they become and writes only the columns that differ, adding and deleting entries, so a rule that moves or renumbers many changes all or none; deleted with its entries; and the collections holding a document among their documents. An entry deleted takes its headnote draft with it, as every delete in the app's editors does, never a document's own summary an entry chose; a collection's write adds a headnote draft alone, refusing any other summary, so no collection write changes what the search reads, and none moves the search mark.
- **`/api/v1/me/collections`** (`Collections.swift`): the list, the most recently changed first; New Collection, in the project the user works in; a collection with its entries, each with its depth in the kit's outline and what its row shows; a change of its own fields, filing it under the project worked in as the app's `recordEdit` does; Delete; Duplicate, the app's `Collection.duplicate(in:)`; a preset, offered by the kit's rule; and `GET /api/v1/me/volumes/{v}/documents/{d}/collections`, for the rail.
- **The entries** (`CollectionEntries.swift`): Add Documents' add and the picker's, which a collection holding the document takes no second time; a heading, a note block and an apparatus block; an excerpt frozen from the page's version or from a highlight's passage; Move, a heading carrying its section; Sort by Date across the collection or within each section; an entry's change, the inspector's inclusions among them; Delete, Delete Section, Indent and Outdent, each where the kit's outline allows it; and the inspector, with what each Default resolves to.
- **The editor's rules** (`CollectionEditing.swift`), the app's, mirrored: its appends, deletes and moves, the outline's normalization and indent rules, `CollectionEntryOrdering` and `sortedByDate`, the appends of `CollectionDocumentDiscovery` and `CollectionExcerpts`, the duplicate, `SmartCollectionRule`, a preset's fields and `matches`, and the inspector's selections and resolved defaults.
- **The browser app:**
  - the Collections tab (`/collections`), in the header on a server that keeps user data: the list, with the app's project banner and Show All; New Collection, the Mac's sheet; Duplicate; and Delete…, which asks first;
  - the editor (`/collections/$collectionId`), the iPad's: Add, a menu with the five apparatus blocks named as the app's submenu is; Sort by Date; Collection settings, the iPad's sheet, each field saved as it is typed; and Contents, each row the app's, a collapsed heading hiding its section, with a menu for what the app's context menu holds;
  - a note block and the introduction in S15d's editor, a note block plain at rest and edited in place;
  - Add Documents, with Search and Browse, and Add Highlighted Passages…;
  - the inspector, for a document and for a section's defaults;
  - the selection bar's Excerpt, between the colours and Note, and the Add to Collection picker in both of its modes;
  - the Research rail's Collections section, closed until it is opened, after Tags;
  - `shell/MenuButton.tsx`, the WAI-ARIA menu button the editor's menus share.

**Decided here, each the web's own**

- **Briefing packet where a summary is stored.** The kit offers Briefing packet, and the Summary only depth, where summaries are available, which the app answers from its generation; this server generates none, so it answers whether a document of the collection has a summary stored that is no draft. S18f refuses the depth where a document has none, with the app's reason.
- **New Collection is the Mac's sheet.** The iPad makes an untitled collection and opens it; the web names one first, as the Mac's sheet does, and the picker's New Collection uses the same sheet.
- **Delete… asks first.** The app deletes a collection by a swipe; a button that deletes at once would be too easy to press by keyboard.
- **Menus for the context menu, and Move Up and Move Down for the drag.** Each row's menu holds what the app's context menu does, and Move Up and Move Down, by the outline's rules, move a heading with its section, a collapsed one hopped whole, where the app drags.
- **A note block is plain at rest.** The editor opens on Edit, or at once for a block just added, and saves as it is typed, half a second after the typing stops or when it is left; the formatting is S15d's.
- **A collection's changes go one at a time, and each shows at once.** The browser sends a collection's changes in turn, each once the one before is answered, and the server's answer is the copy. A switch, a checkbox or a choice shows what was chosen in the moment it is chosen (`chosen.tsx`), and the collection held shows each change until its answer stands, an answer to an earlier change shown with the later ones over it, so a second press reads the first; a refusal reads the collection again.
- **Move Up and Move Down are worked out as they are sent,** from where the moves before them left the row, so a second press before the first is answered moves the row on, and focus a move takes from a row React places anew goes back to its menu.
- **What a change stamps.** A collection's `lastModified` moves when its own fields change or an entry joins or leaves it, and an entry's when it changes, so the list's order is the app's.
- **An entry a newer build wrote stays.** The app's row for one offers nothing, and the server refuses its deletion.
- **The rail's names open the editor, and its header counts them.**
- **The inspector's New Note… and headnote card wait for S18f,** which brings headnotes the researcher writes; the live preview beside the outline waits for S18e's exports.
- **What the server cannot keep it refuses.** A collection's or an entry's text may not hold U+0000, where SQLite's text ends, or pass a note's 1 MiB, as a note's may not; null clears a note, subtitle, author line or title override and is refused for a field that cannot be none; and Summary only, set field by field where Briefing packet's card is refused, is refused as the card is, a depth the collection holds standing.
- **An add past the highest position renumbers first.** The app appends one past the highest position, which an import of an edited file can set at `Int.max`; there the app's arithmetic would trap, and on a server every user shares, so the entries are renumbered in their order first.
- **A draft the server cannot read is left out of a copy.** The app copies an entry's headnote draft whatever it holds; a draft row the export's reader cannot read the web's copy cannot copy, and shared, a delete of either entry would take the other's, so the copy's entry has none.
- **An excerpt holds text.** Where the page's flat text has none between the offsets, as for a selection of spaces, the app freezes the raw selection; the web refuses it, and offers Excerpt for no footnote, by the kit's rule.
- **The inspector's summary is the newest** where none has the collection's prompt, where the app takes the first its fetch returns, in no order it sets.
- **Citations and Tags wait upstream.** Add Documents' Citations tab reads the kit's `CollectionCitationLineResolver`, and its Tags tab the kit's `CollectionGeneratedBlocks.tagDocumentRefs`, both internal to FRUSCoreKit at `32e295e5`. A copy of either would break CLAUDE.md's rule 4, so the sheet has Search and Browse until a pull request on FRUS-Explorer makes them public and a pin move takes it.

The Session Log said "Nothing recorded yet" where the test's visit should have been. That run had not been run again when this pull request opened.

The suite's other tests passed, but for the one it skips in every pass.

**What was wrong.** The app had a race. Since S17f (#84), the reader's arrival effect returned until the user's synced preferences had been read. Only Checklist Mode's list needs them, but the visit's `POST …/history/documents` waited with it, and nothing sent it if the reader was left first. The preferences are asked for only once `GET /api/v1/me` has answered.
- **The first test** leaves the reader for Project Home by a click. On the search page the preferences are asked for alongside six other requests; the test clicks the first result about 20 ms later; the reader's account comes some 50 ms after that; and the test leaves as soon as the heading shows. A preferences answer later than about 70 ms (here; more on CI's slower runner) therefore lost the visit. Project Home read a trail with the search and no visit, and nothing read it again, since nothing had been written.
- **The second test** opens the document with a page load and leaves it with another as soon as its heading shows. Its visit waited on the session, the user and the preferences, one after another, while the heading waited on the session and the document, and the page was closed before the visit was sent.

The server's first backup of `app.db` also ran inside the first failure's 10 s wait, at 18:45:03, 300 s after the server started, because that runner ran about 10% faster than the passing ones. But it began some 4.5 s after the visit would have been written, and its reads, through the backup API on a read-only connection to a WAL store, hold up no writer: it was not the cause.

**How it was found.** A diagnostic spec, never committed, ran the first test's opening with every API request logged against its start, and slowed one request at a time with `page.route`; a second ran the second test's opening as it was on `main`. They ran against a cut-down copy of the smoke test's root pass, on ports of this session's own, with the server's web folder mounted from builds of `main`'s web app and of the fix. The server was `frus-light:race`'s, built from `main` (the build took this worktree's context after the fix's first edit, so its own web app is the fix's).
- **The first test's opening, the preferences answered 150, 250, 400 or 1,500 ms late:** with `main`'s web app, 0 of 20 passed. Each failure was the CI failure: Recent Activity held "Recent Searches, treaties" alone, and the server's trail held no visit. With the fix, 20 of 20 passed.
- **The second test's opening, the preferences answered 100 or 400 ms late:** with `main`'s web app, 0 of 10 passed, each with "Nothing recorded yet"; with the fix, 10 of 10. On time, 5 of 5 on both.
- **The visit's write sent 300 ms or 3 s late, or Project Home answered 300 ms late** (on `frus-light:s23d`, with its own web app): 6 of 6 passed, Project Home reading again once the write was answered.
- **Nothing slowed:** 5 of 5 on both web apps; the first test itself, 30 times on each, passed 30 of 30 at load averages of 3 to 5.

**The fix.** `ReaderScreen.tsx`'s arrival is `recordArrival`, which runs to its end after the reader is left. It sends the visit once the document's account has loaded and the user is known, since the server records it only while Log Research Sessions is on. It awaits the preferences only to take the document off Checklist Mode's list. While the server keeps user data the header's project picker holds the preferences query, so that read outlives the reader too. One behaviour changes: a preferences read that fails no longer drops the visit.

**The spec.** A page closed before the reader has the user cannot send the visit, since a change carries the user's token. So the second test now waits for its visit on the server before it leaves the document, as the file's third test waits for its second search.

**The tests.**
- **A unit test,** `ReaderTrail.test.tsx`'s "records a document left before the user's preferences are read", holds the preferences and leaves the reader for Browse. It fails on `main`'s reader, with no visit sent, and passes with the fix, which then takes the document off the list once the preferences come.
- **A browser test** in `projects-history.spec.ts` holds the search page's preferences until the reader has been left for Browse, and expects the visit in the server's trail. With `main`'s web app it failed 5 of 5; with the fix it passed 5 of 5, and the file's other four tests passed 20 of 20 on both. The browser suite goes from 80 tests to 81 in each pass.
- **The rail's Notes and Summary tests** stub no preferences, so on `main` the reader never sent its visit there. Three of them count every POST; they now leave the visit out (`isVisitRecord`).

**How it was checked:**
- `scripts/npm run typecheck`, `run lint`, `test` and `run build`: clean; 556 tests in 60 files.
- `scripts/compose-smoke --e2e` with `frus-light:race`, which holds this branch's web app byte for byte, on port 18240, passed every step: the browser suite's 81 tests at the root and 81 under the path, 80 passing and the one it skips in each, `projects-history.spec.ts`'s five among them, and the library, accounts and sign-in specs.

**Delivered:** the reader's arrival outliving the reader, the second test's wait, the two new tests and the three narrowed counts, and this log. The diagnostic specs and the harness are in the shared notes folder, under `race-projects-history/`.

**Next:** phase 3's rows go on, as PLAN's Phase 3 section has them, with S23c's pin move after #117 and #115.

## Session 17f: projects, the history and the method appendix

28 October 2026 · branch `claude/jovial-albattani-6a881b` · [#84](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/84) · upstream `32e295e5`, unchanged

Phase 2's row S17f, the third of the search-and-research rows that S17c's pin move opened. A user works in one project at a time, chosen in the header, with the Mac's Project Home for it; the trail records the documents they visit and the searches they run, with the Mac's capture fields, and the History screen, the Session Log and the switch that stops the recording are the app's; the method appendix is the kit's, in Markdown and CSV; and the Mac's synced preferences are each user's, the citation style among them, with the reader's own order of tags and projects. Each is the kit's code where #1805 moved it there, and app code mirrored, held to the app's source, where it is the Mac's view or service. No upstream pull request and no pin move; migration 3 adds one column. One part of the row waits: Project Home's focus subjects, with a lead's snippet, which the kit makes in code it keeps internal, so they need an upstream pull request first.

**What the kit gives,** at `32e295e5`, from FRUS-Explorer#1805:
- `ResearchTrailSessions`: `group(_:idleInterval:)`, a trail's sessions, split after 30 idle minutes, and `newestFirst(_:limit:)`, the window a page of the Session Log reads; `SessionLogSnapshot.page(of:datedActivityCount:limit:)`, with its page limit and increment.
- `QueryMethodAppendix`: `make(recordedSearches:corpusNames:projectName:researchQuestion:generatedAt:corpusCoverage:)`, and `markdown(for:)` and `csv(for:)` for a `Host`, which gives the app's version, the data files, the locale, the calendar and the time zone; `RecordedSearch` and its `RecordedCount`, said by `appendixDescription(locale:)` and `basisToken`; and `Row.scopeProse(resources:locale:)`.
- `DocumentEngagementService.gather(among:forProject:)` and `partition(corpusKeys:keys:isOpenedComplete:)`, with `EngagementCoverage`'s words.
- `ResearchItemCounts.tally` and `ProjectTally.summary`, a project's "12 notes · 3 collections".
- And from earlier pins: `SearchScopeSignature.signature(for:)`, `SearchService.matchExpressions(for:)`, `FTS5InlineQueryParser.normalizingQuotationMarks(_:)`, `CorpusCaptureTruncation`'s line and `CitationStyle`.

**Delivered**

- **The store** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/UserProjects.swift`, `UserTrail.swift`, `UserResearchRows.swift`): migration 3's `users.active_project_id`, the project each user works in, which reads as none once the project is gone; `ProjectStore`'s list, the project worked in, the deletion and the merge, as `ProjectAdminService` does them; `TrailStore`'s pages of the three trail tables, newest first and a row with no time last, the count of dated rows, and the deletions; and `PreferenceStore`'s one row a user, made with `SyncedPreferences()`'s values the first time it is written. S17e's `SearchSetStore` and these now share `ResearchRowStore`, a user's rows read and written as the export and the import map a Mac's record. Their writes change neither `user_search` nor the tag assignments, so they leave the search mark (`writing(outsideSearch:)`), and a search kept outlives a visit's recording.
- **`/api/v1/me/projects`** (`Projects.swift`): the list by name, with each project's tally and the project the user works in; New Project, which makes it that project, as the app's editor does; a project; a change of its name, question or default tags, writing the columns changed alone and stamped; Delete, which returns the user to Global Context if it was theirs and leaves the trail's rows as they were; Merge, `POST …/{id}/merge`, which files the notes and collections under the target, re-points the visit plans, the summaries and the three trails, moves the user to it if they worked in the source, and leaves the leads; and `GET` and `PUT /api/v1/me/active-project`. `PROJECT_NOT_FOUND` for a project not the user's.
- **Project Home** (`ProjectHome.swift`): `GET /api/v1/me/projects/{id}/home`, the app's `ProjectHomeSummary` over the store's rows: the counts; each corpus's coverage by the kit's engagement rules, with Log Research Sessions read as whether the opened count is complete; the focus tags; the leads not dismissed, by their score, NEW for a week, and a lead's editorial-note flag as the user's corrections leave it; and the five newest visits, notes and searches. `POST …/leads/{id}/dismiss` dismisses one.
- **The trail** (`History.swift`): `GET /api/v1/me/history`, a page of each table for a scope, each visit's title as the app's `ReadingHistoryTitle` gives it, and each search's count and scope in the appendix's words; `POST …/history/documents`, a visit, stamped with the project the user works in; `POST …/history/searches`, the server's own run of the search the screen ran, with the Mac's capture fields, refreshing the row the anchor names when its words are the same, as `SearchHistoryWriter` does; the deletion of a row and of the whole trail; `GET …/history/sessions`, the Session Log, with the Research Sessions pane's summary (`ResearchSessionsSummary`); and `GET …/history/appendix`, the method appendix as an attachment, in Markdown or CSV, its dates in the zone the browser names. While Log Research Sessions is off, the two records are `suppressed`.
- **The synced preferences** (`Preferences.swift`): `GET` and `PATCH /api/v1/me/preferences`, the Mac's `SyncedPreferences` record for each user, with `SyncedPreferences()`'s values for one who has set nothing. A change writes the fields it names, a list replacing that list alone in the Mac's payload (`ListOrderPreferences`), and a style or a mode the app has not is refused. The import and the export carry the record whole, as S16d made them.
- **The browser app:**
  - the header's project picker, with Project Home and Manage Projects, and "Working on:" over Browse and Search;
  - Project Home (`/projects/$projectId`): the question, saved as it is typed; the date focus; the tiles and the coverage; the focus tags; Suggested Next, with Dismiss, the focus going on to the next lead; and Recent Activity;
  - History (`/research/history`), beside All Notes, with its scope, its search field, Show More and Delete;
  - in Settings: Projects, with the editor, New Project…, Delete and Merge; Research Sessions, with the switch, the Session Log (`/settings/sessions/log`) and Delete Recorded Sessions…; Reading, with Open Documents In and the citation style; Data's method appendix, a link for each file; and Move to Top, Move Up and Move Down in Tags and Projects, whose order the tag picker, the note editor, My Tags and the project picker follow;
  - the reader's record of each arrival at a document, the mode a document opens in, and Cite's style, the user's;
  - Search's record of each search it runs, and Checklist Mode's line while the switch is off;
  - Export as JSON headed by the project the user works in, as the app's export sheet heads it.

**Decided here, each the web's own**

- **The project a user works in is theirs, on the server.** The Mac keeps it on each device, and a browser is any device, so the web keeps one for each user, in a column of its own in `users`, which no Mac record carries and no import changes. None is Global Context.
- **A search's record is the server's run of it.** The screen sends the search and the row it last wrote, and the server runs the search again for the Mac's capture fields: the exact count, the user's half included; the rows kept, up to the ceiling of 7,500; the ceiling; the volumes indexed; the scope's signature; the corpus; and the expression it compiled to. So a record is what the API answers, not what a browser says. A search with no words, or one the server refuses, is recorded not at all.
- **The anchor is the tab's.** The Mac's `SearchHistoryWriter` keeps the row it last wrote for its window; the browser keeps it for the tab's session, a reload included, in `sessionStorage`, so the same words run again refresh that row, and a return to a search's results records nothing again. The records go one at a time, each with the anchor the one before it answered, as the Mac's writer moves its anchor at once, and one the server could not take is tried again the next time its run is shown.
- **Remember Last reads the browser.** Open Documents In is synced, but the research panel's last state, which Remember Last reopens, stays in each browser, as the Mac keeps it on each device.
- **The citation style moves once.** The style the browser kept before S17f goes to the server once for the browser, the first time anyone's preferences are read in it, if the server holds none for them; no second user and no import that empties a style takes it. After that the server's is the style, and while the user's are read Cite shows the style this browser last chose, so a citation does not open in another first.
- **A change shows at once.** A preference, and the project the user works in, show the new value before the server answers, in every control that shows them, and the server's copy stands once the newest change is answered, or, if the server refuses it, its copy as it was. An older answer that arrives after a newer change was sent is not taken as the copy.
- **The appendix's host is the server's, and its zone the browser's.** The Generated line names "FRUS Explorer Light" and the server's version; the scopes are said with the server's data files, in US English and the Gregorian calendar, as the server's other words are; and the dates are in the time zone the browser names, since the server's is not the reader's.
- **The exports wait for S18e.** The trail's third table holds the exports an import brings; the web's own exports are collections', and S18e keeps each in the history.
- **A visit the index cannot title takes the reader's title from its TEI.** The app titles a visit by the head it parsed (`DocumentViewModel.readingHistoryTitle`), with the kit's `IndexingPipeline.extractHeader(from:)`, which is internal. The server takes the index's head where the index holds the document; for one it does not hold, as front matter is, or for any while no index is served, it takes the title the reader shows for it (`DocumentDetail(teiOnly:)`): "Preface", or "Document 3".
- **Focus subjects and a lead's snippet wait upstream.** Project Home's subjects come from the kit's `VolumeSubjectProfiles`, and a lead's snippet from `IndexingPipeline.documentSnippets(forKeys:)`, both internal to FRUSCoreKit at `32e295e5`. A copy of either would break CLAUDE.md's rule 4, so Project Home leaves both out until a pull request on FRUS-Explorer makes them public and a pin move takes it.

**Tests**

- **FRUSLightCoreTests,** 158 to 162: `UserTrailTests`, 4 on each store: the project a user works in, theirs and gone with it; a merge, re-pointing what the app's merge re-points; a trail page, newest first in its scope, with the dated count and the deletions; and the preferences' row, made once and changed by field, with a merge that reads the row as the write finds it. `UserStoreConformanceTests`' test of the search mark now holds S17f's writes to leaving it.

- **FRUSParityTests,** 203 to 206: `ProjectHistoryParityTests`, 3: every Mac word the web takes, about 170, under its key in the app's source and in copy.ts's block; the reader's own order, the History screen's filter, Project Home's and "Working on:"'s lines and the checklist's, the app's code and the web's mirrors of it, with the kit's quotation marks; and the server's mirrors of the app's views and services.
- **The web unit suite,** 356 to 392 tests in 38 to 42 files: `s17fRules.test.ts`, `ProjectsAndHistory.test.tsx` (Project Home, each project's question its own and a refused save sent again; the picker and a choice shown at once; History, its Delete's and Show More's focus and the way in from All Notes; Project Home read again after a note or a tag; and the record of a search, one at a time and kept for the tab's session), `S17fSettings.test.tsx` (Projects, Research Sessions, the Session Log, Reading, a change shown at once and put back on a refusal, the style given once for the browser, and Data's appendix) and `ReaderTrail.test.tsx` (a visit recorded once, the switch and Checklist Mode, Open Documents In, and Cite's style while the preferences are read); `ResearchRail.test.tsx`'s Remove… with a frame before the rows are drawn again; and the panes S17f changed.
- **The browser suite,** 53 to 57 tests, at the root and under the path: `projects-history.spec.ts`, with axe, makes a project by keyboard, works in it and sees its Project Home and, reached from All Notes, its History fill; turns the trail off, reads the Session Log and deletes the trail; downloads the method appendix in both formats for two recorded searches, one that found nothing; and keeps the citation style and the mode documents open in as the user's own. **Decided here, each the web's own**

Nothing of it is stored.

- **The capture is the server's.** The rows a search shows can be 7,500, more than a body under `/me` takes, so the browser names the search and the reviewed, and the server captures its retained rows; it also says what the Mac's sheet says before Save, so the sheet shows the server's own count.

- **What a recall here cannot carry is said.** A Mac's saved search can set `booleanMode`, a person in one volume, a project or a topic, which the API does not take; the sheet's row says a recall runs without them, and its count is of the whole search.
- **Rename and Delete of a corpus, and Delete Scope,** which the Mac keeps in its Settings, are in Browse, beside the drill and the editor, where the web lists them.
